title: Road accidents: reporting and police abstract — general guidance
citation: Traffic Act, Cap. 403; National Police Service guidance
content: Report accidents to police promptly, obtain the OB number and later the police abstract, and seek medical care with P3 forms where injured. Take scene photos, number plates, witness contacts, and insurance details. Insurers usually require prompt notification.

title: Adoption and guardianship — general guidance
content: Adoption and guardianship require court orders and agency or children's officer assessment focused on the child's welfare. Informal handover of children without court process does not confer legal parental responsibility. Keep birth records, assessment reports, and court orders.

title: Mediation and alternative dispute resolution — general guidance
content: Courts encourage mediation, arbitration, and traditional dispute resolution where appropriate, which can be faster and cheaper than trial. Settlement agreements should be written and, where needed, adopted as court orders. Keep settlement drafts and attendance records.

title: Affordable Housing Levy payroll handling — general guidance
content: Employers handle Affordable Housing Levy deductions and remittance through KRA systems alongside payroll taxes. Correct payroll setup and timely filing avoid penalties. Keep levy declarations and payment records with monthly payroll.

title: Fake agents and double letting — general guidance
content: Confirm an agent's authority and view the house before paying deposits, and insist on receipts in the landlord's or agency's name. Double letting and viewing-fee scams should be reported to police. Keep listings, messages, payment proof, and IDs used.

title: Appeals from magistrates to High Court — general guidance
content: Decisions of magistrates courts and some tribunals may be appealed to the High Court within statutory timelines. The appellant files a memorandum of appeal with the judgment and proceedings. Keep the appeal filing receipt and stay orders if any.

title: Court of Appeal and Supreme Court path — general guidance
content: Further appeals go to the Court of Appeal and, on defined constitutional or certified questions, to the Supreme Court. Leave or certification may be required before filing. Keep lower-court records and appellate directions together.

title: Appeals — general guidance
content: Dissatisfied parties may appeal to a higher court within short, strict deadlines running from judgment or ruling. Appeals require the judgment, proceedings, and grounds. Get advice immediately after judgment and keep the decree and filing receipts.

title: Arbitration and conciliation outside court — general guidance
content: Parties with arbitration clauses or mutual consent may use private arbitration or conciliation instead of litigation. Awards may be recognised and enforced through the courts. Keep the arbitration agreement and award documents.

title: Arrest and detention — general guidance
citation: Constitution of Kenya, 2010, Art. 49; Criminal Procedure Code
content: Arrested persons have rights: to be informed of reasons, to remain silent, to legal representation, to be brought before court within 24 hours, and to bail or bond where applicable. Police must not use excessive force. Note the station, OB number, officers involved, and time of arrest.

title: Assault and theft — general guidance
content: Assault and theft are criminal offences. Victims should report to police, obtain medical attention and a P3 form where injured, and keep records such as photos, receipts, and witness contacts. The Director of Public Prosecutions handles prosecution.

title: Auctioneers and repossession — general guidance
content: Auctioneers must act on lawful instructions with proper notice and identification, and sales require advertisement. If goods are seized, demand the proclamation, notice, and auctioneer's licence details, and seek urgent legal help. Keep loan, notice, and payment records.

title: Bail and bond — general guidance
citation: Constitution of Kenya, 2010, Art. 49; Criminal Procedure Code
content: An arrested or accused person has the right to bail or bond on reasonable conditions unless there are compelling reasons to deny it. Conditions and amounts vary by offence and court. Keep bail receipts, surety documents, and hearing dates, and confirm conditions with the court or lawyer.

title: Paying the balance and handing over a motor vehicle — general guidance
content: Pay the balance only when you are ready to take possession, verify documents, and start the TIMS transfer process. Record the handover date, mileage, fuel, spare keys and accessories in a signed handover note. Keep the handover note, final receipt and transfer initiation evidence.

title: Beat licences and split sheets — general guidance
content: Beat sales and free downloads are governed by licence terms covering exclusivity, streams, credit, and resale. Without a written licence, disputes turn on messages and payment proof. Always use split sheets naming beatmakers, writers, and percentage shares. Keep licences and payment records.

title: AGPO certificates for youth, women, PWDs
content: AGPO reserves tenders for youth, women, and persons with disabilities with renewable certificates. Apply with IDs and business records. Keep certificates and renewal dates.

title: Agrovet shop requirements
citation: Pest Control Products Act; veterinary guidance
content: Agrovets need trained staff and board licensing with safe storage of chemicals. Verify supplier authorisation. Keep licences and stock records.

title: Company annual returns on BRS
content: Companies file annual returns with current directors, shares, and registered office. Late filing attracts penalties. Keep filing receipts and registers.

title: Beneficial ownership register
content: Companies maintain beneficial ownership records of significant controllers with BRS filings. Update on share changes. Keep registers and filing receipts.

title: Running a boda fleet
content: Fleet owners document hire terms, maintenance, insurance, and instalments per bike with rider IDs. Keep agreements and payment records.

title: Butchery licences and meat inspection
content: Butcheries need slaughter and inspection compliance with cold-chain records. Source from licensed slabs. Keep licences and inspection stamps.

title: Cafes and noise compliance
content: Music and generators must respect night-noise limits with NEMA permits for events. Keep permits and complaint responses.

title: Car wash water and location rules
content: Car washes need authorised water sources, drainage, and county permits away from road reserves. Keep permits and water bills.

title: Chama constitution essentials
content: Constitutions state membership, contributions, leadership, loans, and dispute handling with meeting rules. Register where opening accounts. Keep minutes and ledgers.

title: Closing a business properly
citation: Companies Act; BRS and KRA guidance
content: Settle debts, taxes, and dues, notify staff and creditors, and file dissolution or cessation. Keep clearance certificates and filings.

title: Customer data duties for shops
content: Shops holding customer contacts need consent, limited collection, and secure records with deletion on request. Register where thresholds apply. Keep consent records.

title: Collecting business debts
content: Send itemised demands with invoices and delivery proof, then mediate or file in small claims. Keep LPOs, delivery notes, and acknowledgement messages.

title: Changing directors or address
content: File director, secretary, and address changes on BRS with resolutions within timelines. Keep minutes and filing receipts.

title: Dismissing fairly in small businesses
content: Even small employers must give notice, reasons, and hearings before termination. Document warnings and minutes. Keep contracts and termination letters.

title: Employee theft and fraud
content: Theft by staff needs stock audits, OB reports, and fair disciplinary process with hearings. Keep audit reports, statements, and hearing minutes.

title: Petrol station licensing
content: Fuel retail needs EPRA licences with safety, calibration, and environmental compliance. Apply with site plans. Keep licences and calibration records.

title: eTIMS exemptions and thresholds
content: Confirm current eTIMS onboarding bands and exemptions on KRA guidance before trading without invoices. Keep the KRA determination and sales records.

title: Fire clearance for business premises
content: Premises handling crowds, fuel, or kitchens need fire inspection and certificates with extinguishers. Book inspection early. Keep certificates and inspection reports.

title: Food business licences and medicals
citation: Public Health Act; Food and Drugs Act
content: Food handlers need medical certificates with premises meeting hygiene standards. Renew medicals periodically. Keep certificates and inspection reports.

title: Hawking and street trading permits
content: Street traders need county permits for zones and hours with fee receipts. Trade only in designated areas. Keep permits and receipts.

title: Validating a business idea in Kenya
content: Test demand, pricing, and costs with small pilots before registering or borrowing. Survey customers and track margins. Keep pilot sales and expense records.

title: Influencer and creator taxes
content: Content income is taxable with PIN, records, and returns; brands deduct withholding where applicable. Keep contracts and payment records.

title: Insuring stock and premises
content: Cover fire, burglary, and liability per stock values with updated schedules. Disclose material facts. Keep policies and valuation records.

title: KEBS standardisation marks for products
content: Manufactured goods need KEBS certification and marks before sale with factory inspection. Apply with samples and labels. Keep certificates and test reports.

title: Applying for liquor licences
citation: Alcoholic Drinks Control Act; county laws
content: Outlets apply for national and county licences with premises, hours, and location vetting. Renew before expiry. Keep licences displayed and renewal receipts.

title: Market stall allocation and fees
content: Stalls allocate through the county with allocation letters and daily or monthly fees. Keep allocation documents and fee receipts for enforcement checks.

title: Milk bars and dairy handling
content: Milk handling needs pasteurisation, cold chain, and Kenya Dairy Board compliance. Keep supplier records and test results.

title: M-Pesa agency: float and fraud
content: Agents manage float, tills, and ID verification with CCTV and receipting to deter fraud. Reconcile daily. Keep float records and incident reports.

title: Name search and reservation on BRS
content: Reserve the business name on BRS through eCitizen with alternatives and fees. Approval precedes registration. Keep the reservation and payment receipts.

title: Registering staff for NSSF and SHIF
content: Register employees promptly and remit monthly with payroll records. Confirm active cover for staff. Keep registration and remittance receipts.

title: Running an online shop
content: List exact items, prices, delivery fees, and return terms with traceable payments. Honour delivery promises. Keep order and delivery records.

title: Partnership deed essentials
content: Deeds record capital, profit sharing, signatories, drawings, and exit terms with dispute clauses. Sign before trading. Keep the deed and contribution records.

title: Payroll taxes checklist for employers
citation: Income Tax Act; SHIF, NSSF, AHL laws
content: Remit PAYE, SHIF, NSSF, and housing levy per payroll calendars with returns. Late remittance attracts penalties. Keep payroll and remittance receipts together.

title: Single business permit renewals
citation: County Governments Act; county finance acts
content: Renew the county permit annually before expiry with the fee for the business size and zone. Display the licence. Keep yearly licences and receipts.

title: Opening a pharmacy or chemist
content: Chemists need superintending pharmacists and Pharmacy and Poisons Board licensing with controlled storage. Apply with premises plans. Keep licences and prescription records.

title: POS machines and settlement
content: Card settlements need provider contracts with fee and settlement timelines. Reconcile daily batches. Keep contracts and settlement reports.

title: Posho mill licensing and KEBS flour
content: Mills need county licences, machine safety, and KEBS-compliant packaging with weights. Keep licences and test records.

title: Opening a salon or barbershop
content: Salons need county licences, sterilised tools, and trained staff with client records for reactions. Keep licences and medical certificates.

title: Supplying schools: contracts
content: School supplies need LPOs, delivery notes, and payment schedules signed by authorised officers. Verify signatories. Keep delivery and payment records.

title: Transferring company shares
content: Share transfers use transfer forms, board approval, stamp duty, and register updates. Keep transfer forms, duty receipts, and updated registers.

title: Bidding compliantly for tenders
content: Bids need tax compliance, business permits, CR12, and technical sheets in sealed formats by the deadline. Late bids are rejected. Keep submission receipts.

title: Challenging tender awards
content: Aggrieved bidders seek administrative review within short standstill timelines with bid and award records. Act immediately. Keep award notices and review filings.

title: Finding public tenders
content: Track tenders on the PPRA portal and supplier registration with AGPO certificates where eligible. Meet submission formats strictly. Keep registration and bid receipts.

title: Tobacco retail rules
content: Tobacco sales face display, advertising, and smoke-free zone restrictions with age limits. Train staff on compliance. Keep supplier invoices and licences.

title: Wines and spirits outlet rules
content: Outlets observe hours, age, and location rules with displayed licences. Train staff on compliance. Keep licences and supplier invoices.

title: Withholding tax on suppliers
citation: Income Tax Act; Tax Procedures Act
content: Payers deduct withholding on rents, professional fees, and imports per schedules and remit with certificates. Issue certificates to payees. Keep deduction records.

title: Business Premises Rent Tribunal — general guidance
citation: Landlord and Tenant (Shops, Hotels and Catering Establishments) Act; Tribunal guidance
content: The Business Premises Rent Tribunal resolves disputes over controlled business premises, including rent changes and termination notices. Parties must follow notice periods set by law before seeking tribunal orders. Keep tenancy agreements and termination notices on file.

title: Using motor dealers and brokers — general guidance
citation: General contract guidance; Consumer Protection Act, 2012
content: Confirm whether the person selling is the owner, a licensed dealer or a broker acting for someone else. Ask for written authority to sell and verify it against the NTSA owner record. Keep the authority letter, dealer receipts and broker communications.

title: Registering a company through BRS — general guidance
citation: Companies Act, 2015; Business Registration Service Act, 2015
content: A company is formed by reserving a name and filing incorporation documents with the Business Registration Service, after which a certificate of incorporation is issued. The company must keep a registered office and statutory registers of members, directors and charges. Keep the certificate and filed returns together for bank, KRA and licensing use.

title: Business names and permits — general guidance
citation: Business Registration Service Act, No. 15 of 2015
content: Sole proprietorships and partnerships register business names through the Business Registration Service, then obtain county single business permits and tax registration. Keep registration certificates, permits, and KRA PIN records.

title: Business name registration for sole traders — general guidance
content: A person trading under a name other than their own must register the business name with BRS before trading. The certificate shows the owner, business name, address and nature of business. Keep the certificate displayed or available for county and bank verification.

title: Protected business tenancies — general guidance
citation: Landlord and Tenant (Shops, Hotels and Catering Establishments) Act, Cap. 301
content: Certain shop, hotel and catering tenancies have statutory protection against termination without notice and access to the Business Premises Rent Tribunal. Rent increases and termination must follow the statutory process. Keep tenancy notices and Tribunal orders with the lease file.

title: Chama, welfare group and self-help registration — general guidance
citation: Community Groups Registration guidance; Micro and Small Enterprises Act, 2012
content: Many chamas register as self-help groups, community groups or societies to open bank accounts and hold property in the group name. A written constitution should state membership, contributions, leadership, meetings and dispute handling. Keep membership lists, minutes and contribution records.

title: Chiefs, elders and community resolution — general guidance
citation: Traditional dispute resolution; legal aid guidance
content: Minor civil disputes, especially family and boundary matters, can often start with chiefs or elders for faster local resolution. Record any agreement in writing with witnesses. Serious criminal matters must still go to police.

title: Chiefs and elders community resolution — general guidance
citation: National Government Coordination Act; ADR guidance
content: Chiefs and village elders help resolve local disputes over boundaries, family matters and minor claims through dialogue. Unresolved or serious matters are referred to courts or relevant offices. Keep any written settlement or referral letter issued.

title: Child custody and maintenance — general guidance
content: Custody, access, and maintenance decisions prioritise the best interests of the child. Both parents have a duty to maintain children according to means. Keep birth certificates, school fee receipts, medical bills, and records of support paid or received.

title: Children Act, 2022
content: The Children Act provides for the care, protection, and rights of children, including parental responsibility, custody, guardianship, foster care, adoption, and protection from abuse and neglect. Decisions prioritise the best interests of the child. Keep birth certificates, school and medical records.

title: Children's Court and child protection — general guidance
content: Children's courts handle custody, maintenance, protection and offences involving children, with priority on the best interests of the child. Matters may be reported through children's officers or police. Keep birth certificates, school records and prior orders available.

title: Civil Procedure Act
content: The Civil Procedure Act and rules govern instituting and conducting civil suits, including pleadings, interim orders, injunctions, hearings, and enforcement of judgments. Procedure is technical; verify filing fees, forms, and timelines on the e-filing portal or with legal aid.

title: Closing or transferring a business — general guidance
content: Closing or selling a business involves settling debts, taxes, employee dues, and deregistration or transfer filings. Notify creditors and staff in writing and keep clearance certificates. Verify the checklist with BRS and KRA.

title: Music collective management (MCSK, KAMP, PRISK) — general guidance
content: Kenyan music rights are administered through licensed collective management organisations for authors, producers, and performers. Registration and membership affect royalty collection. Keep membership records, work declarations, and royalty statements.

title: Broker commission on motor sales — general guidance
content: Agree broker commission in writing before the sale, stating the amount or percentage, when it is payable, and who pays it. Avoid paying commission before the logbook transfer is underway. Keep the commission agreement and payment receipts.

title: Community Land Act, 2016
content: Community land is held by communities and managed through registered community assemblies and committees. Transactions require community consent procedures. Verify registration status and minutes of consent with the community register and county office.

title: Companies Act, 2015 — overview
content: The Companies Act governs incorporation, directors' duties, shares, and filings through the Business Registration Service. Compliance includes annual returns and proper records. Verify registration and compliance status on the BRS portal before transacting.

title: Directors duties and company records — general guidance
content: Directors must act within the articles, exercise care and diligence, and avoid conflicts of interest. Companies must file annual returns and notify BRS of changes in directors, shareholding and registered office. Keep minutes, registers and filings updated for compliance checks.

title: Buying a motor vehicle from or for a company — general guidance
content: A company sale should be authorised by a director or resolution, and the signatory should prove authority to sell on behalf of the company. Confirm the company is active and that the vehicle is not pledged to a lender. Keep board authority, company search, agreement and transfer records.

title: Unexplained airtime deductions
content: Unsubscribed VAS deductions are disputed with the provider for refund and opt-out, then CA. Keep deduction messages and complaint numbers.

title: Hidden bank charges
content: Banks must disclose fees; dispute unexplained debits in writing with statements. Escalate to CBK with complaint references. Keep statements and tariff sheets.

title: Betting payout disputes
citation: Betting, Lotteries and Gaming Act, Cap. 131
content: Payout disputes turn on bet slips, terms, and account logs. Complain to the operator then BCLB with records. Keep tickets and transaction histories.

title: Expiring data bundles and airtime
citation: Kenya Information and Communications Act; CA guidance
content: Bundle terms on expiry and rollover follow provider terms filed with CA. Complain first to the provider, then CA with reference numbers. Keep purchase messages and complaint tickets.

title: Escalating telecom complaints to CA
content: After 30-day provider non-resolution, escalate to CA with the provider reference, account, and evidence. Keep every ticket and response.

title: Car hire damage claims
content: Hire terms state excess, inspection, and fuel rules with pre-hire photos. Inspect jointly on return. Keep the hire agreement and inspection sheets.

title: Veterinary negligence and pet loss
content: Negligent treatment claims need records, bills, and a second opinion. Complain to the practice and the veterinary board. Keep treatment cards and receipts.

title: Chama money lost by officials
content: Missing chama funds are demanded with contribution records and minutes, then reported as theft or breach. Keep M-Pesa records, minutes, and member lists.

title: Spotting counterfeit goods
content: Check KEBS marks, packaging, and seller authorisation; prices far below market signal fakes. Report to ACA and KEBS with samples. Keep receipts and seller details.

title: Lost parcels with couriers
content: Couriers insure per declared value with tracking. Declare value, keep the waybill, and claim in writing with contents proof. Escalate to CA where ignored.

title: Escalating energy complaints to EPRA
content: Unresolved distributor complaints escalate to EPRA with meter numbers, bills, and reference history. Keep the full correspondence file.

title: Event cancellations and ticket refunds
content: Cancelled events trigger refund per promoter terms with timelines. Claim in writing with tickets and payment proof. Keep adverts and cancellation notices.

title: Expired food on shelves
citation: Food, Drugs and Chemical Substances Act
content: Report expired or relabelled food to public health with outlet name, receipt, and photos. Seek care where illness follows. Keep treatment records.

title: Delayed flights and lost luggage
content: Report baggage loss immediately at the desk for a PIR, then claim with tags and receipts. Keep boarding passes and the PIR.

title: Unfinished fundi work after deposit
content: Demand completion in writing with a deadline before engaging another fundi, then claim the extra cost. Keep quotations, deposit proof, and progress photos.

title: Furniture orders and deposits
citation: Consumer Protection Act; Sale of Goods Act
content: Furniture LPOs state design, timber, dimensions, delivery date, and balance terms. Inspect before final payment. Keep designs, receipts, and delivery notes.

title: Cooking gas refills and safety
content: Refill at licensed dealers, check seals and weights, and keep cylinders upright and ventilated. Report illegal refilling to EPRA. Keep purchase receipts.

title: Gym and club membership cancellations
content: Memberships renew per signed terms with cancellation notice rules. Cancel in writing and stop auto-pay. Keep contracts and cancellation proof.

title: House deposits to fake agents
content: Verify the house, agent authority, and landlord identity before paying deposits, and receipt to the landlord account. Report fraud with listings and messages. Keep all payment proof.

title: Repudiated insurance claims
content: Insurers must give written repudiation reasons. Respond with policy, premium proof, and loss evidence, then complain to IRA. Keep claim numbers and correspondence.

title: Job offer fee scams
content: Legitimate employers never charge placement fees. Verify company registration and offices before paying. Report with adverts, messages, and payment proof.

title: Reporting to KEBS and ACA
content: Reports attach samples, receipts, and seller details to KEBS for standards and ACA for counterfeits. Keep acknowledgement references for follow-up.

title: Disputing high electricity bills
content: Compare meter readings with bills, test for faults, and lodge written disputes with meter photos before disconnection. Escalate to EPRA with references. Keep bills and readings.

title: Token meter tampering allegations
content: Tampering allegations lead to back-billing and disconnection; demand inspection reports and test results in writing. Keep bills, inspection notes, and payment records.

title: Shop goods seized by landlord
citation: Distress for Rent Act; tenancy guidance
content: Shop stock attachment must follow distress procedure with inventory. Irregular seizures are challenged urgently in court or tribunal. Keep stock lists and seizure records.

title: Advocate fee disputes
content: Fees follow fee schedules and engagement letters with taxation at the High Court where disputed. Ask for written fee notes upfront. Keep engagement letters and bills.

title: SIM registration problems
content: Unregistered or wrongly registered lines face suspension. Register with original ID at authorised agents. Keep registration confirmations.

title: Digital lender harassment in collection
content: Abusive calls and contact-list shaming violate licensing and data rules. Report to CBK and ODPC with recordings and messages. Keep loan statements and proof of payments.

title: Matatu overcharging and receipts
content: Fares should match gazetted or displayed rates with ticketing. Report overcharging with route, plate, and time to NTSA and police. Keep tickets and photos.

title: Mechanic overcharging and part swaps
content: Agree diagnostics, parts, and labour in writing with old parts returned. Dispute in writing with a second quote. Keep job cards and receipts.

title: Delayed M-Pesa to wrong number
content: Use reversal channels immediately for wrong sends and never resend to callers pressuring you. Report fraud to the provider and police. Keep transaction codes.

title: Verifying phones before buying
content: Check IMEI, box, receipt, and seller identity; test calls, cameras, and charging. Avoid blacklisted or iCloud-locked devices. Keep seller ID and payment proof.

title: Private hospital billing disputes
content: Request itemised bills, compare with admission estimates, and dispute in writing with the accounts office. Escalate to regulators where overcharged. Keep bills and medical reports.

title: Always demand a receipt or ETR slip
citation: Consumer Protection Act, 2012; Tax Procedures Act
content: Receipts prove price, date, and seller for every warranty or refund claim. eTIMS invoices add tax verification. Photograph receipts before ink fades and keep digital copies.

title: Refurbished phones and laptops
content: Sellers must disclose refurbished status, battery health, and warranty length. Get the condition in writing. Keep the disclosure and test results.

title: Earnest money for plots and houses
content: Earnest payments need written refund, forfeiture, and timeline terms before transfer steps. Pay traceably to verified accounts. Keep agreements and receipts.

title: SACCO dividend delays
content: Dividends follow audited accounts and AGM resolutions with payment schedules. Raise delays with the society in writing, then SASRA. Keep statements and AGM minutes.

title: Salon injuries and reactions
content: Allergic reactions and burns need prompt care with product names recorded. Complain in writing to the salon and public health. Keep treatment records and product details.

title: School fee refunds on withdrawal
citation: Basic Education Act; consumer contract terms
content: Refunds follow the admission terms and fee policy with written withdrawal notice. Claim in writing with receipts. Keep admission letters and payment records.

title: School transport safety complaints
citation: Traffic Act; NTSA school transport rules
content: School vans need licensed drivers, speed governors, and seat belts with vetted crew. Report violations to the school and NTSA with plate and route. Keep fee receipts.

title: Suing a shop in Small Claims Court
content: Defective-goods claims within the monetary limit file with receipts, warranties, and demand letters at the registry. Confirm current limits before filing. Keep the claim and service copies.

title: Solar kit pay-as-you-go disputes
content: Solar PAYG terms state deposit, instalments, and switch-off rules. Confirm warranty and servicing before signing. Keep contracts and payment histories.

title: Tailor and fundi deposits
content: Agree fabric, measurements, price, and delivery date in writing with deposit receipts. Breaches are demanded in writing first. Keep samples and messages.

title: Ride-hailing disputes and safety
content: Screenshot trip details, route, and fare before disputing with the app. Report safety incidents to the app and police. Keep trip records and messages.

title: Failed token purchases
content: Unreceived tokens after payment are traced with the transaction code, meter number, and time. Report to the vendor and Kenya Power. Keep M-Pesa confirmations.

title: Travel agents and cancelled trips
content: Package terms state cancellation tiers and refund timelines. Verify licensing and bookings directly. Keep itineraries, receipts, and cancellation notices.

title: Warranties on electronics and appliances
content: Warranties state duration, exclusions, and service centres in writing. Register products and report defects within the window. Keep warranty cards and service job sheets.

title: Disputing water bills
content: Test meters, check leaks, and dispute in writing with readings and photos. Pay undisputed amounts to avoid disconnection. Keep bills and plumber reports.

title: Filing an access-to-information request
content: Write to the information access officer describing the records sought, pay any prescribed fee, and keep proof of delivery. The body must respond within the statutory period. If refused, seek review by the Commission on Administrative Justice.

title: Constitution of Kenya, 2010 — Article 43
content: Article 43 recognises economic and social rights including accessible and adequate housing, reasonable standards of sanitation, health care, and social security. These rights are subject to progressive realisation and may only be limited as provided by law. Verify how a specific claim maps to this article with a legal aid provider.

title: Constitution of Kenya, 2010 — Article 47
content: Article 47 guarantees fair administrative action that is expeditious, efficient, lawful, reasonable and procedurally fair. A person affected by administrative action is entitled to written reasons. Keep copies of the decision, the notice received, and any written reasons given.

title: Constitution of Kenya, 2010 — Article 48
content: Article 48 requires the State to ensure access to justice for all persons. Where a person cannot afford legal representation and the interests of justice so require, representation may be provided at the State's expense. The National Legal Aid Service toll-free line is 0800 720 640.

title: Constitution of Kenya, 2010 — Article 50
content: Article 50 guarantees the right to a fair hearing, including having disputes resolved in a fair and public hearing before a court or tribunal. Accused persons have related rights including to be informed of the charge, to legal representation, and to bail where applicable. Verify procedure with a lawyer.

title: Rights and fundamental freedoms — scope
content: Article 19 explains that rights belong to individuals, preserve dignity, and bind the State and, where applicable, private persons. Limits must be justified under Article 24. When relying on a right, identify the specific article and how the facts fit it, then seek legal aid to test the claim.

title: Application of the Bill of Rights
content: Article 20 requires courts to interpret rights to favour their enforcement and to consider values like human dignity and equality. A person alleging a violation can go straight to the High Court. Keep a dated account of events, witnesses, and any documents showing the violation.

title: Implementation of rights and State duties
content: Article 21 obliges the State to observe, respect, protect, promote and fulfil rights, with progressive realisation for socio-economic rights within available resources. When petitioning an office, cite the duty and attach evidence of requests already made. Keep stamped copies of every petition.

title: Enforcing the Bill of Rights in court
content: Article 22 lets any person alleging a rights violation apply to the High Court for redress, and associations may act in the public interest. Formalities should be kept to a minimum. File a petition with an affidavit, the facts, the rights infringed, and the orders sought.

title: Relief the High Court may grant
content: Under Article 23 the High Court may declare rights violated, issue injunctions, order compensation, or grant conservatory orders to preserve the position pending hearing. Ask a lawyer which orders fit the urgency. Keep the petition, affidavits, and any interim orders together.

title: When rights may be limited
content: Article 24 permits limits only by law that is reasonable and justifiable in an open and democratic society, considering the nature and purpose of the limit. Some rights, such as freedom from torture, cannot be limited. Challenge any limit by asking the authority to cite the exact law.

title: Rights that cannot be limited
content: Article 25 protects freedom from torture and cruel treatment, slavery, and the right to a fair trial as non-limitable. Violations should be reported to police, IPOA where officers are involved, and a lawyer immediately. Preserve medical evidence and witness details.

title: Equality and freedom from discrimination
content: Article 27 guarantees equality before the law and bans discrimination on grounds including race, sex, pregnancy, disability, and religion. Affirmative action for marginalised groups is allowed. Record dates, comparators, and documents when lodging an equality complaint.

title: Human dignity protection
content: Article 28 declares every person has inherent dignity that must be respected and protected. Degrading treatment by officials or employers can ground complaints to oversight bodies and courts. Document what was said or done, where, and who witnessed it.

title: Freedom and security of the person
content: Article 29 protects against arbitrary detention, bodily harm, and psychological torture. Anyone detained must be told reasons and produced in court within 24 hours. Note the station, OB number, officers involved, and time of arrest for any follow-up.

title: Freedom from slavery and forced labour
content: Article 30 prohibits slavery, servitude, and forced labour. Workers held through threats, withheld documents, or debt bondage can report to police and the labour office and seek shelter support. Keep contracts, messages, and payment records as evidence.

title: Privacy as a constitutional right
content: Article 31 protects against search of person, home or property, seizure of possessions, and infringement of communications. Searches generally need lawful authority. Ask officers to identify the law and warrant, and note details without obstructing. Complain afterwards with a lawyer.

title: Freedom of conscience and religion
content: Article 32 protects freedom of conscience, religion, belief and opinion. No one may be compelled to act against belief except as law reasonably requires. Schools and employers should accommodate belief within reason. Put accommodation requests in writing.

title: Freedom of expression and its limits
content: Article 33 protects expression, media freedom, and academic freedom but excludes propaganda for war, incitement to violence, hate speech, and advocacy of hatred. Online posts can attract criminal complaints. Preserve links and timestamps and seek advice before responding publicly.

title: Freedom of the media
content: Article 34 guarantees media independence and bars State control over broadcasts or penalties for opinions. Complaints about media content go to the Media Complaints Commission. Keep broadcasts, articles, and dates when filing or answering a complaint.

title: Right of access to information
citation: Constitution of Kenya, 2010, Art. 35; Access to Information Act, 2016
content: Article 35 and the Access to Information Act let citizens request information held by the State and relevant private bodies. Requests go in writing to the information officer with a clear description. Keep the request copy, delivery proof, and the response deadline.

title: Assembly, demonstration and picketing
content: Article 37 protects peaceful assembly, demonstration and picketing. Organisers should notify police as required by the Public Order Act and keep events peaceful and unarmed. Carry the notification copy and organisers contacts during the event.

title: Political rights of citizens
content: Article 38 protects every citizen's right to form parties, contest elections, vote by secret ballot, and stand for office. Electoral disputes have strict timelines before the IEBC tribunal and election courts. Keep voter records, results forms, and objection receipts.

title: Freedom of movement and residence
content: Article 39 guarantees citizens freedom of movement, residence anywhere in Kenya, and the right to leave and return. Restrictions such as curfews must be lawful and published. Note the order relied upon and seek review if it seems unlawful.

title: Protection of the right to property
content: Article 40 protects the right to acquire and own property, with compulsory acquisition allowed only for public purpose with prompt full compensation. Do not surrender land without a written acquisition notice. Keep title deeds, valuations, and all notices.

title: Labour relations as a constitutional right
content: Article 41 guarantees fair labour practices, reasonable working conditions, the right to join unions, and the right to strike subject to law. Dismissals and union disputes can go to the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Keep contracts, payslips, and dispute correspondence.

title: Right to a clean and healthy environment
content: Article 42 guarantees a clean and healthy environment. Pollution, illegal dumping, and noisy operations can be reported to NEMA and county environment officers. Keep dated photos, a diary of incidents, and report reference numbers.

title: Economic and social rights claims
content: Article 43 covers health, housing, food, water, social security, and education. Claims proceed through petitions showing the State failure and the remedy sought. Attach prior complaints to the responsible office and their responses.

title: Language and cultural rights
content: Article 44 protects the right to use one's language and participate in cultural life. Cultural practices that violate rights, such as forced marriage, remain unlawful. Report harmful practices to chiefs, children officers, or police.

title: Family as the natural unit of society
content: Article 45 recognises the family as the fundamental unit of society and gives every adult the right to marry a person of the opposite sex with free consent. Parties to a marriage enjoy equal rights during and after marriage. Register marriages to protect property and children's rights.

title: Consumer rights in the Constitution
content: Article 46 gives consumers rights to goods of reasonable quality, information, health and safety, and compensation for loss from defective goods. This backs claims under the Consumer Protection Act. Keep receipts, warranties, and defect evidence.

title: Rights of arrested persons in detail
content: Article 49 requires an arrested person to be informed of reasons in an understandable language, allowed to contact counsel, and brought to court within 24 hours. Statements should not be forced. Memorise or note badge numbers, station, and OB entry.

title: Rights of detained and imprisoned persons
content: Article 51 preserves the dignity of detained persons including access to family, counsel, and medical care. Complaints about treatment go to the prison authorities, IPOA where relevant, and KNCHR. Keep visit records and medical notes.

title: Commission on Administrative Justice (Ombudsman)
citation: Constitution, Art. 59; Commission on Administrative Justice Act, 2011
content: The Ombudsman handles complaints about unfair, slow, or unresponsive public administration, such as delayed IDs, pensions, or land files. Complain first to the office, then to the Commission with reference numbers. Keep stamped copies and timelines.

title: National Gender and Equality Commission
content: The NGEC addresses gender, disability, youth, and minority discrimination in public and private institutions. Complaints should state the discriminatory act, dates, and witnesses. Keep policies, letters, and meeting notes as evidence.

title: Kenya National Commission on Human Rights
citation: Constitution of Kenya, 2010, Art. 59; KNCHR Act
content: The KNCHR investigates human rights violations, visits detention places, and can recommend redress. Complaints are lodged in writing with facts, dates, and evidence. Keep the complaint reference and follow-up correspondence.

title: Bill of Rights — general guidance
content: Chapter Four of the Constitution protects fundamental rights including equality, dignity, privacy, expression, and property. Rights may be limited only by law that is reasonable and justifiable. Enforcement is through the courts; keep a written record of what happened, when, and who was involved.

title: Delayed birth certificates
citation: Births and Deaths Registration Act, Cap. 149
content: Applications for birth certificates go through civil registration with hospital notification and parent IDs. Follow up in writing with the application number where delayed. Keep notification slips and payment receipts.

title: Complaining about a chief or assistant chief
content: Misconduct by a chief, such as demanding bribes for letters, can be reported to the Deputy County Commissioner with specifics. Keep copies of the request, any payment evidence, and witness names.

title: Petitioning a county assembly
content: Any person may petition a county assembly on matters within its authority, such as markets, health, or local roads. Petitions state facts, the relief sought, and attach evidence. Keep the filed copy with the clerk stamp.

title: County governments — general guidance
citation: Constitution of Kenya, 2010; County Governments Act, No. 17 of 2012
content: Many services such as business permits, markets, parking, and local rates are handled by county governments. Disputes about county fees or enforcement should start with the county office notice and receipts, then escalate through internal appeal or legal aid. Keep every receipt and notice.

title: County revenue and rate demands
citation: County Governments Act; county finance acts
content: County rate and fee demands state the property, period, and amount with payment points. Dispute errors in writing with receipts. Keep demand notes and payment records.

title: Devolution and which government to approach
citation: Constitution of Kenya, 2010, Ch. 11; County Governments Act, 2012
content: National government handles matters like immigration, tax, and courts while counties handle markets, local roads, health facilities, and business permits. Directing a complaint to the wrong level causes delay. Check the function list before filing and keep the referral letter.

title: Double allocation of market stalls
content: Where two traders hold papers for one stall, the county allocation register and fee receipts decide priority. Report to the market office with all documents and avoid taking the space by force. Keep allocation letters and payment records.

title: Checking voter registration details
content: Voters should verify registration status and polling station during the inspection period using IEBC channels. Report errors early with ID copies. Keep screenshots and correction receipts.

title: Demanding written reasons for admin action
citation: Constitution, Art. 47; Fair Administrative Action Act, 2015
content: A person affected by administrative action may demand written reasons. Make the demand in writing referencing the decision, date, and officer. The reasons reveal whether to appeal, seek review, or go to court.

title: Service complaints at Huduma Centres
content: Delays or demands for unofficial payment at service centres should be reported through the centre manager and the Huduma call line with the ticket number. Keep the service ticket, receipts, and names of officers seen.

title: Delayed national ID processing
content: First ID applications need a birth certificate, school documents, and chief introduction. Track the waiting slip and follow up at the registration office. Keep copies of all documents submitted.

title: Electoral complaints to IEBC
content: Election offences and registration problems can be reported to IEBC officials and monitors with polling station details and evidence. Formal election petitions go to the designated courts within strict timelines. Keep voter slips, results photos, and report numbers.

title: Judicial Service Commission complaints
content: Complaints about judicial officers go to the JSC in writing with the case number, dates, and conduct complained of. Matters pending in court should still be pursued through appeal or review. Keep filings and hearing records.

title: National Land Commission complaints
citation: Constitution, Art. 67; National Land Commission Act, 2012
content: The NLC investigates historical land injustices and monitors public land use. Complaints need the parcel details, history, and supporting documents. Keep title copies, maps, and correspondence with the lands office.

title: Land, environment and property rights — overview
content: The Constitution protects the right to property and sets principles for land policy including equitable access and security of land rights. Compulsory acquisition requires prompt and full compensation. Land disputes are commonly handled through the land registry, the Environment and Land Court, or alternative dispute resolution.

title: Public Service Commission recruitment disputes
content: Public service appointments must follow fair competition and merit. Candidates alleging bias can seek internal review with the advertisement, shortlist, and scores. Keep application receipts and interview invitations.

title: Nyumba Kumi community policing
citation: National Police Service community policing guidance
content: Nyumba Kumi clusters share security alerts with police and chiefs through cluster heads. Join the local cluster and save emergency contacts. Keep meeting notes.

title: Public finance complaints and county budgets
citation: Constitution, Ch. 12; Public Finance Management Act, 2012
content: Counties must publish budgets and allow public participation before spending. Residents can request budget documents and submit memoranda during participation forums. Keep adverts, submissions, and attendance records for any challenge.

title: Notifying police of a public meeting
content: Organisers of public meetings or processions should notify the police in writing in advance with the venue, route, date, and contacts. Carry the acknowledgement on the day. If restricted, ask for written reasons and consult a lawyer.

title: Public participation and petitions — general guidance
content: Public bodies must facilitate public participation, and every person has the right to petition public authorities. Put complaints and petitions in writing, keep a stamped copy, and note reference numbers and response dates for follow-up.

title: Salaries and Remuneration Commission queries
content: The SRC sets public officers pay and reviews allowances. Queries about public salary grading go through the employer and SRC advisories. Keep appointment letters, payslips, and grading correspondence.

title: Teachers Service Commission discipline
content: The TSC registers teachers and handles discipline and transfers. Teachers facing interdiction should respond in writing within the given time and attach evidence. Keep the show-cause letter, response, and hearing notices.

title: Using ward and sub-county offices
content: Ward administrators and sub-county officers handle local disputes, bursaries, and referrals with stamped records. Start there before headquarters. Keep referral slips.

title: Consumer complaints — general guidance
content: Complain first in writing to the seller with receipt, photos, and a clear remedy and deadline. If unresolved, escalate to the sector regulator or seek legal aid and small claims advice. Keep the full correspondence trail.

title: Consumer Protection Act, 2012
content: The Consumer Protection Act shields consumers from unfair practices, defective goods, and misleading advertising, with remedies including repair, replacement, refund, and compensation. Keep receipts, warranties, adverts, and written complaints with dates.

title: Consumer refunds — general guidance
content: Consumers are entitled to goods of merchantable quality and services carried out with reasonable care. Remedies include repair, replacement, or refund depending on the defect and timing. Keep receipts and records of the defect and return attempts.

title: Essentials of a valid business contract — general guidance
content: A binding contract generally requires offer, acceptance, consideration and intention to create legal relations. Terms may be written, oral or implied from conduct, but written terms are easier to prove. Keep signed contracts and any variations in writing.

title: Contracts — general guidance
content: Most business and personal agreements should be in writing with parties, price, timelines, delivery, and termination terms. Oral deals are harder to prove. Keep signed copies, payment proof, and messages showing variations.

title: No automatic cooling-off for motor purchases — general guidance
content: There is generally no automatic right to return a vehicle simply because you changed your mind after signing. Cancellation depends on what the written agreement says and whether the seller misrepresented the vehicle. Keep the signed agreement and all pre-sale messages and adverts.

title: Co-operative Tribunal for SACCO disputes — general guidance
content: Disputes concerning SACCO membership, deposits, loans and guarantor liability may be filed before the Co-operative Tribunal. Claims should attach by-laws, statements, loan forms and demand correspondence. Keep Tribunal pleadings and orders with the loan file.

title: Co-operatives Tribunal disputes — general guidance
content: The Co-operatives Tribunal hears disputes between co-operatives, members and officials concerning management, loans and elections. Claims are filed with society records and relevant resolutions. Keep membership records and tribunal filings together.

title: Copyright Act, 2001 — overview
content: The Copyright Act protects original literary, musical, artistic, and audio-visual works, including beats, songs, and recordings, against unauthorised reproduction and distribution. Protection arises on creation, but registration helps prove ownership. Keep project files, dated exports, and registration certificates.

title: Market stalls and street trading — general guidance
content: Market stalls, kiosks and street trading spaces are allocated and regulated by the county, often with daily, weekly or monthly fees. Allocation letters and fee receipts prove lawful occupation. Keep allocation documents and fee receipts for inspection.

title: County parking and loading zones — general guidance
content: Counties regulate on-street parking, loading bays and clamping or towing for non-compliance in urban areas. Delivery vehicles should use designated loading zones and display payment where required. Keep parking receipts and any clamping release documents.

title: County business permits and enforcement — general guidance
content: Trading without a current single business permit risks closure and penalties. Verify fee schedules at the county office, display permits, and keep payment receipts. Challenge enforcement actions through receipts and written appeal rather than confrontation.

title: County land rates — general guidance
citation: Rating Act, Cap. 267; Valuation for Rating Act, Cap. 266
content: Owners of rateable property pay annual land rates based on the county valuation roll and finance act rates. Arrears may attract penalties and enforcement against the property. Keep rate demands, valuation notices and payment receipts.

title: County single business permit — general guidance
citation: County Governments Act, 2012; county finance acts
content: Businesses operating in a county must obtain the applicable single business permit or trade licence before opening and renew it annually. The fee depends on business size, sector and location under the county finance act. Keep the licence displayed and renewal receipts filed.

title: Court-annexed mediation — general guidance
content: Courts may refer suitable civil and family cases to accredited mediators for a time-bound settlement attempt. Successful mediation is recorded as a consent order. Keep the mediation referral and any settlement agreement.

title: Appealing a criminal conviction or sentence
content: Convictions and sentences can be appealed within short statutory timelines. Get the judgment, proceedings, and charge sheet immediately and brief counsel. Keep filing receipts and bail-pending-appeal papers where applicable.

title: Arson and property destruction
content: Deliberately setting fire to buildings, crops, or vehicles is arson with severe penalties. Report immediately, preserve the scene for investigators, and list destroyed property with values. Keep photos and ownership documents.

title: Assault occasioning actual bodily harm
content: Fights causing injury should be reported with a P3 form for medical documentation. Get treatment first, then the police issue the P3 for the doctor to complete. Keep treatment notes, photos, and witness contacts.

title: Reviewing harsh bail or bond terms
content: Accused persons unable to meet bail can apply for review with reasons and surety details. Courts consider flight risk, offence gravity, and means. Keep the bail ruling, receipts, and review application copies.

title: Boda boda and motorbike theft
content: Report stolen motorbikes with registration, engine and chassis numbers, and tracker data where fitted. Alert stages and mechanics with photos. Keep logbook copies, sale agreements, and OB records.

title: Burglary and housebreaking
content: Breaking into homes or shops to steal attracts burglary charges. Preserve the scene where possible, photograph forced entry, and list stolen items with values and receipts. Report the same day for OB entry.

title: Cattle rustling and banditry
citation: Penal Code; National Police Service operations guidance
content: Rustling and bandit attacks should be reported immediately with locations, numbers, and movement direction for security response. Communities should use peace committees and early warning. Keep OB numbers and loss lists.

title: Child neglect and abandonment
content: Failing to provide for a child or abandoning one can attract criminal and care proceedings. Report to children officers and police with birth records and evidence of neglect. Keep school, medical, and support-payment records.

title: Child sexual exploitation material
citation: Sexual Offences Act; Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act
content: Creating or sharing sexual images of children is a grave offence. Do not forward such material; report to police and the DCI child-protection units with links and handles. Keep report references safely.

title: Demands for bribes by officials
citation: Anti-Corruption and Economic Crimes Act, 2003; Bribery Act, 2016
content: Demands for bribes for services, licences, or release can be reported to EACC with dates, amounts, and recordings where lawfully obtained. Do not pay to speed up a right. Keep receipts and reference numbers.

title: Fake currency encounters
citation: Penal Code; Central Bank of Kenya Act
content: Notes suspected to be counterfeit should not be re-spent. Report to police and the bank with details of who gave them. Keep the transaction records and suspect description.

title: Cyber harassment and non-consensual images
content: Sharing intimate images without consent, cyberbullying, and threats online are offences. Preserve links with timestamps, report to the platform and police, and seek support services. Do not delete evidence.

title: Defilement of children: urgent steps
content: Defilement cases need immediate medical care, preferably within 72 hours, and prompt police reporting. Do not wash away evidence before examination. The child needs counselling, a children officer referral, and legal aid. Keep medical and OB records.

title: Assault within the home: immediate steps
citation: Protection Against Domestic Violence Act, 2015; Penal Code
content: Seek safety and medical care first, then report to police for OB and P3 documentation. Protection orders can bar the abuser from the home. Keep medical records, photos, and witness details.

title: Drug possession and trafficking
citation: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1994
content: Possession and trafficking of narcotics attract severe penalties with limited bail options for trafficking. Anyone arrested should get counsel immediately and note the search and seizure details. Keep charge sheets and hearing dates.

title: Child marriage is prohibited
content: Marriage of a person under 18 is prohibited and voidable. Threatened marriages can be stopped through children officers, chiefs, and courts. Keep birth records, school records, and any ceremony plans as evidence.

title: Unlicensed guns and imitation firearms
content: Possession of firearms without a certificate, including imitation guns used in robberies, is a serious offence. Report armed sightings with descriptions and direction of movement without confronting. Keep report references.

title: Abuse and exploitation of older persons
content: Beating, neglecting, or grabbing property of older persons can be reported to chiefs, police, and social development officers. Arrange medical care and safe custody of documents. Keep medical and property records.

title: Obtaining by false pretences (wash-wash style fraud)
content: Con tricks promising jobs, tenders, or forex in exchange for fees are obtaining by false pretences. Stop further payments, preserve chats and receipts, and report to police and DCI. Keep adverts and suspect contacts.

title: FGM as a criminal offence
citation: Prohibition of Female Genital Mutilation Act, 2011
content: FGM, aiding it, or taking a girl across borders for it are offences. Suspected plans can be reported to police, chiefs, children officers, or helplines before the act. Keep any messages, plans, and witness details safely.

title: Forgery of documents
content: Making or using false title deeds, agreements, or certificates is forgery. Suspected forgeries should be reported with originals, the suspect documents, and transaction history. Keep registry search results and payment proof.

title: Protection orders for GBV survivors
content: Survivors can seek court protection orders barring contact, occupation, or tenancy interference. Applications are supported by affidavit evidence and police reports. Breach of an order is itself an offence. Keep the order and breach evidence.

title: Grievous harm and serious injury
content: Serious injuries such as fractures or deep wounds are prosecuted as grievous harm with heavy penalties. Hospital records and the P3 form are central evidence. Keep admission records, X-rays, and expense receipts.

title: Hate speech and incitement reports
content: Ethnic contempt, incitement, and hate leaflets can be reported to police or the NCIC with recordings and witness details. Keep originals of posts, broadcasts, and rally details for investigators.

title: Human trafficking indicators and reporting
content: False job offers, confiscated passports, and locked accommodation signal trafficking. Victims and witnesses can report to police, the counter-trafficking secretariat, or helplines. Keep messages, contracts, travel documents, and payment records.

title: Identity theft and fake IDs
citation: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, 2018; Penal Code
content: Use of another person's ID for loans or SIM registration is identity theft. Victims should report to police and DCI, notify lenders and CRB, and dispute fraudulent accounts in writing. Keep affidavits and dispute letters.

title: Illicit brew and unlicensed alcohol
content: Manufacturing or selling chang'aa or unlicensed alcohol is an offence enforced with county officers and police. Report dens to chiefs and police rather than confronting sellers. Keep report references.

title: Kidnapping and abduction response
content: Report missing or abducted persons immediately with photos, clothing details, last location, and phone data. Police can seek call data through proper channels. Keep the OB number and investigating officer contacts.

title: Reporting lost documents and items
content: Lost IDs, certificates, and number plates should be reported promptly for an OB entry and police abstract needed for replacement. Keep the abstract copy for the registrar or NTSA.

title: Malicious damage to property
content: Damaging windows, fences, crops, or vehicles can be charged as malicious damage. Photograph the damage, get repair estimates, and report with ownership proof. Keep receipts for all repairs.

title: Mob justice is a crime: what to do
content: Beating or killing suspects is murder or assault regardless of the accusation. Witnesses should report to police and preserve photos safely. Communities should hand suspects to lawful custody.

title: M-Pesa reversal and fraud scams
content: Fake reversal calls and wrong-number refunds are common fraud. Never share PINs, verify balances independently, and report with transaction codes to the provider and police. Keep SMS records and call reference numbers.

title: Murder and manslaughter procedure
citation: Penal Code, Cap. 63; Criminal Procedure Code
content: Homicide cases begin with immediate police report, scene preservation, and post-mortem examination. Only the High Court tries murder. Families should get the OB number, post-mortem report access, and legal aid early.

title: Online shopping and social media fraud
content: Fake online sellers vanish after payment. Screenshot listings, seller profiles, till numbers, and chats before they disappear, then report to the platform, provider, and DCI. Keep payment confirmations.

title: Stolen phones: IMEI and tracking
content: Report phone theft with the IMEI, block the SIM with the provider, and give police the box and purchase receipt. Court orders may be needed for tracking data. Keep the OB number and provider references.

title: Plea bargaining in criminal cases
citation: Criminal Procedure Code; ODPP plea-bargain guidelines
content: Accused persons may negotiate pleas with the prosecution through counsel, subject to court approval. Agreements must be voluntary and informed. Never plead without understanding the sentence. Keep the agreement and court record.

title: Assault by police: where to complain
content: Excessive force, shootings, or deaths in custody can be reported to IPOA with station, date, OB details, and medical evidence. Parallel complaints may go to KNCHR. Keep medical reports, photos, and witness contacts.

title: Reporting rape and adult sexual assault
content: Survivors should reach safety, seek medical care, and report to police for P3 and statement recording. Counselling and PEP treatment have strict time windows. Keep clothes worn, messages, and witness details for investigators.

title: Police clearance certificate (good conduct)
content: Good-conduct applications run through eCitizen with fingerprints at designated centres. Delays are followed up with the application reference. Keep the payment receipt and fingerprint acknowledgement.

title: Robbery and violent theft
content: Robbery involving force or threats is a grave offence with severe penalties. Victims should seek safety and medical care first, then report with descriptions, plate numbers, and recovered items. Do not confront armed suspects.

title: Shoplifting and supermarket theft
content: Shop theft is prosecuted with CCTV, recovered goods, and staff testimony. Suspects should cooperate with police and seek counsel early. Keep the OB entry and charge sheet copies.

title: SIM-swap fraud response
citation: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, 2018; KICA
content: Sudden loss of network followed by strange withdrawals signals SIM swap. Contact the telco to freeze the line, notify banks, and report to DCI with IDs and transaction records. Keep reference numbers from every office.

title: Stock theft and livestock movement
citation: Penal Code; livestock movement permit rules
content: Stolen cattle, goats, and sheep cases need ownership marks, photos, and movement records. Report the same day and alert neighbouring markets and slaughter points. Keep branding certificates and sale records.

title: Attempted suicide: help not punishment
content: Persons in crisis need urgent care, counselling, and helpline support rather than stigma. Contact emergency services, counsellors, or helplines such as 1199 or 0800 720 640 referrals. Keep referral records for follow-up care.

title: Theft: reporting and what police need
content: Theft of phones, livestock, or household goods should be reported promptly with serial numbers, purchase receipts, and witness names. Obtain the OB number and follow up with the investigating officer. Keep the OB slip and any recovery documents.

title: Threats to kill or harm
content: Written or uttered threats of death or injury are offences. Preserve messages with timestamps, report to police, and request advice on protection. Keep screenshots, call logs, and witness names.

title: Night trespass and prowling
content: Lurking around homes at night with intent can be charged as night trespass. Report with times, descriptions, and CCTV where available. Improve lighting and locks while police investigate.

title: Victim impact statements at sentencing
content: Victims may present impact statements on harm suffered before sentencing. Prepare the statement with medical, financial, and emotional effects. Keep expense receipts and reports to attach.

title: Wildlife and charcoal offences
citation: Wildlife Conservation and Management Act, 2013; Forest Conservation Act
content: Poaching, bushmeat trade, and illegal logging or charcoal burning attract heavy fines and jail terms enforced with KWS and KFS. Report quietly with locations and vehicle details. Keep report numbers.

title: Witness protection for serious crimes
content: Threatened witnesses in serious cases can seek protection through the Witness Protection Agency via police or ODPP. Report threats immediately with details. Keep threat evidence and agency references.

title: Wrongful arrest and malicious prosecution
content: Arrests without cause or fabricated charges can ground compensation claims after acquittal. Note every detail of the arrest, bond, and trial outcome. A lawyer assesses prospects once proceedings conclude.

title: Escalating cases through DCI and ODPP — general guidance
citation: National Police Service Act; Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions Act
content: Complex or stalled criminal complaints in Kenya can be escalated from the police station to DCI offices, with prosecution decisions made independently by the ODPP. Complainants can follow up in writing and request reasons for delays or decisions. Keep OB numbers, statements, and all follow-up letters.

title: Hate speech and NCIC complaints — general guidance
content: Hate speech and incitement along ethnic, racial, or religious lines are prohibited in Kenya and can be reported to police or the National Cohesion and Integration Commission. Online posts, broadcasts, and public rallies can all form the basis of complaints. Keep screenshots, recordings, and report reference numbers.

title: P3 forms and medical evidence after assault — general guidance
content: Victims of assault or sexual offences in Kenya should seek prompt medical care and have injuries documented through a police-issued P3 form completed by a medical officer. Early treatment and documentation help preserve evidence even where reporting is delayed. Keep hospital notes, P3 forms, and OB numbers.

title: Criminal procedure — general guidance
content: Criminal cases generally start with a report to police, investigation, arrest or summons, plea, hearing, and judgment. An accused person should be informed of the charge, may seek bail or bond, and should get legal representation early. Keep the charge sheet, bond documents, and hearing dates.

title: Wildlife offences and KWS enforcement — general guidance
content: Poaching, trafficking in trophies, and unauthorised entry into protected areas attract serious penalties enforced with Kenya Wildlife Service support. Community members can report suspicious activity to KWS or police without confronting suspects. Keep report numbers and any permits or receipts.

title: Customs and import basics for traders — general guidance
citation: East African Community Customs Management Act, 2004
content: Importers need a PIN, clearance through a licensed clearing agent and payment of applicable duties and taxes before release of goods. Prohibited and restricted goods require permits from relevant agencies. Keep import entries, permits and duty receipts for audit.

title: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, 2018 — overview
citation: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, No. 5 of 2018
content: The Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act criminalises unauthorised access, interception, fraud, identity theft, and publication of false or intimate content. Preserve device logs, screenshots with URLs and dates, and report promptly to police or DCI. Do not delete evidence.

title: Data Protection Act, 2019 — overview
content: The Data Protection Act regulates collection and use of personal data, requiring lawful basis, purpose limitation, and data subject rights including access, correction, and deletion. Controllers and processors may need to register with the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner. Keep consent records and data policies.

title: Acknowledging debt without restarting time
content: Careless acknowledgements can restart limitation. Mark payments as without prejudice where advised and get counsel before signing. Keep advice notes.

title: Attachment of salary or property
content: Execution attaches salary or goods through court warrants with notice. Challenge irregular execution promptly. Keep warrants, notices, and payment proof.

title: Auction notices and redemption
content: Auctions need proclamation, advertisement, and notice periods; owners may redeem before the fall of the hammer. Verify the auctioneer licence. Keep notices and valuation reports.

title: Bankruptcy as a last resort
content: Bankruptcy writes down debts but restricts credit, travel, and offices for years. Get advice before petitioning. Keep creditor lists and asset records.

title: Challenging irregular repossession
content: Repossessions without agreement process, notice, or licensed agents are challengeable with urgent court orders. Note agents, vehicles, and time. Keep the loan file and seizure evidence.

title: Chama loan defaults
content: Chama defaults follow the constitution with demand, guarantor calls, and mediation. Keep contribution records, minutes, and demand letters.

title: Debt collection and demand letters — general guidance
citation: General contract and civil procedure guidance
content: Creditors should demand payment in writing with the amount, basis, and deadline before filing suit. Debtors should respond in writing, verify the debt, and propose terms rather than ignoring letters. Keep agreements, statements, and all correspondence.

title: Administration for struggling companies
content: Administration protects viable companies while rescuing or winding down with practitioner control. Directors act fast on advice. Keep management accounts and creditor lists.

title: Mediating debt disputes
content: Courts may refer debt cases to mediation for structured repayment consent orders. Prepare income and creditor schedules. Keep mediation agreements.

title: CRB clearance certificates
content: After clearing arrears, obtain a clearance certificate and confirm bureau updates before applying for loans. Keep settlement letters and clearance copies.

title: Disputing a wrong CRB listing
content: Request your clearance report, dispute errors in writing with payment proof to the bureau and lender, and escalate to CBK where unresolved. Keep dispute letters and reference numbers.

title: Credit card debt and statements
content: Reconcile interest, fees, and minimum dues on statements monthly. Dispute errors in writing with the bank. Keep statements and dispute references.

title: Replying to a demand letter
content: Answer demand letters in writing within the deadline, admitting, disputing, or proposing payment with evidence. Silence invites suit. Keep the letter, reply proof, and payment records.

title: Checking digital lender licences
content: Borrow only from CBK-licensed digital lenders with disclosed fees and interest. Verify licensing on CBK lists. Keep screenshots of terms and disbursement messages.

title: Employer loans on resignation
content: Employer advances are set off against final dues with itemised statements within deduction limits. Demand the computation. Keep loan forms and clearance records.

title: Loans taken in your name by fraud
citation: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act; Penal Code
content: Report fraudulent loans to the lender, CRB, and DCI with affidavits and IDs. Dispute the debts in writing. Keep affidavits, OB numbers, and dispute letters.

title: Called as a guarantor: steps
content: Demand the principal statements, default notice, and your guarantee cap before paying. Liability follows the signed guarantee terms. Keep the guarantee and all demand letters.

title: Harambee pledges as debts
content: Public pledges can be enforceable depending on reliance and wording. Honour or renegotiate in writing. Keep pledge records and communications.

title: HELB penalties and compliance
content: Default penalties accrue on missed instalments; compliance certificates aid employment clearance. Negotiate catch-up plans in writing. Keep statements and clearance.

title: HELB repayment and clearance
content: HELB loans accrue per award terms with employer check-off and self-payment options. Request statements and clearance after repaying. Keep award letters and payment records.

title: Hire purchase defaults and repossession
content: Hirers in default face repossession per the Act with protected-payment rights. Demand statements and notices before surrender. Keep the agreement and payment receipts.

title: Hospital bill payment plans
content: Hospitals allow written instalment plans against detained documents disputes; detention of bodies over bills is unlawful. Negotiate with itemised bills. Keep bills and plan letters.

title: Instalment orders after judgment
content: Courts set monthly instalments on income evidence where lump payment is impossible. Apply with budgets and proof. Keep the order and payment receipts.

title: Interest and penalty disclosures
content: Lenders must disclose total cost, penalties, and default consequences upfront. Challenge undisclosed charges in writing. Keep adverts, agreements, and statements.

title: After judgment: paying by instalments
content: Judgment debtors may apply to pay by instalments with income evidence. Honour orders to avoid execution. Keep the decree and payment records.

title: KRA tax debt and agency notices
content: KRA may issue agency notices to banks and debtors for unpaid tax. Object within timelines with returns and payment proof. Keep assessments, objections, and receipts.

title: Deposit set-off against rent arrears
content: Deposits may be set off against proven arrears or damage with an itemised statement, not blanket forfeiture. Challenge unsupported deductions. Keep ledgers and statements.

title: Legal aid for auction threats
content: Borrowers facing auction of homes or tools of trade can seek NLAS help with loan files and notices. The toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Keep statements and sale adverts.

title: Logbook loans and repossession
content: Logbook lenders register interests and may repossess on default with notice. Read the agreement on valuation and sale. Keep the agreement, statements, and repossession notices.

title: Blacklisting threats by lenders
content: Threatening messages should be verified against actual bureau status; listing needs notice. Dispute wrongful listings. Keep messages and bureau reports.

title: M-Shwari, KCB M-Pesa and Fuliza arrears
