content: Telco-bank overdrafts deduct from wallets on receipt; statements show balances and fees. Clear actively to protect CRB standing. Keep statements and repayment confirmations.

title: Negotiating penalty waivers
content: Seek written waivers of penalties with lump-sum offers and hardship proof. Record any deal before paying. Keep offer letters and settlement receipts.

title: Negotiating repayment plans — general guidance
content: Propose realistic repayment plans in writing, ask for statements and waiver of penalties where possible, and never sign blank documents. If sued, attend court and present payment evidence. Keep proof of every payment made.

title: Overdrafts and bounced cheques
citation: Banking practice; Penal Code on fraud
content: Unauthorised overdrafts attract fees; knowingly issuing bad cheques risks prosecution. Regularise limits in writing. Keep mandates and correspondence.

title: KRA payment plans
content: Taxpayers may seek instalment plans with reasons and cash-flow proof. Honour agreed dates to avoid enforcement. Keep the plan letter and payment receipts.

title: Rent arrears recovery by landlords
content: Landlords recover arrears through demand, distress procedure, or tribunal and court claims with ledgers. Tenants answer with payment proof. Keep ledgers and demands.

title: SACCO deposits attached for loans
content: Societies may offset deposits against defaulted loans per by-laws. Reconcile statements and dispute errors in writing. Keep membership statements and offset notices.

title: SACCO guarantor liability
citation: SACCO Societies Act; Co-operative Societies Act
content: Guarantors cover defaulted SACCO loans per by-laws and guarantee forms. Request statements and default notices before paying. Keep guarantee forms and payment records.

title: Loan deductions from salary limits
content: Deductions need written authority within statutory take-home limits. Challenge excess deductions with payroll. Keep deduction forms and payslips.

title: School fee arrears and exams
content: Schools should not bar candidates from exams over arrears; negotiate written plans with the board. Keep fee structures, receipts, and plan letters.

title: Family land facing auction
content: Charged ancestral land auctions attract spousal consent and notice defences. Seek urgent legal help with the charge and notices. Keep title, statements, and sale adverts.

title: Unlicensed shylocks and illegal seizure
content: Seizing household goods or IDs without court process is unlawful even where money is owed. Report forceful seizures to police. Keep loan messages and seizure evidence.

title: Limitation periods on debt recovery
content: Contract debts generally must be sued within six years, with acknowledgements restarting time. Verify the applicable period with a lawyer early. Keep dated agreements and payment records.

title: Sued for debt in Magistrates Court
content: Larger debts file as civil suits with plaints and supporting documents. File a defence within timelines. Keep service documents and hearing notices.

title: Sued for debt in Small Claims Court
content: Small debts file with agreements, statements, and demand letters for faster hearing. Defend with payment proof before the date. Keep pleadings and receipts.

title: Supplier debts and LPO claims
citation: Sale of Goods Act; contract guidance
content: Suppliers prove LPOs, delivery notes, and invoices for payment claims. Debtors verify deliveries before paying. Keep the full document chain.

title: Tala, Branch and app loan disputes
content: Dispute balances with in-app statements, disbursement proof, and repayment records. Escalate unresolved cases to CBK. Keep screenshots and references.

title: Verifying a loan before paying
content: Ask for the loan agreement, statements, and computation of balances and penalties before paying alleged arrears. Verify the lender CBK licence. Keep statements and correspondence.

title: Defamation on social media — general guidance
citation: Defamation Act, Cap. 36; Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act
content: False published statements harming reputation may lead to civil defamation claims or criminal complaints for false publications. Preserve posts, shares, and harm evidence, seek retraction in writing first, and verify deadlines with a lawyer before filing.

title: Demand for unpaid invoices — general guidance
content: Where an invoice is overdue, a written demand stating the amount, invoice numbers, due date and a deadline for payment creates a clear record. Delivery by email and physical copy helps prove receipt. Keep proof of delivery and any partial payment acknowledgements.

title: Deposits for motor vehicle purchases — general guidance
citation: General contract guidance; Consumer Protection Act, 2012
content: Any deposit should be recorded in writing with the amount, whether it is refundable, the deadline for balance payment, and what happens if either side defaults. Pay deposits through traceable means and get a receipt. Keep the deposit agreement and payment confirmation.

title: Disputes after motor vehicle sale — general guidance
citation: Consumer Protection Act, 2012; General dispute resolution guidance
content: If defects, unpaid loans or failed transfer emerge after purchase, start with a written complaint to the seller with evidence and a reasonable deadline. Unresolved matters may go to negotiation, mediation or court depending on value and facts. Keep the agreement, search, payment proofs, photos and all correspondence.

title: Divorce and separation — general guidance
content: Divorce procedure depends on the type of marriage and grounds set out in law. Courts may make orders on custody, maintenance, and matrimonial property. Seek counselling or mediation first where safe, and keep marriage certificates, financial records, and evidence of separation.

title: Documents to keep for any case — general guidance
content: For any legal issue keep identification, contracts, receipts, messages, photos, OB or reference numbers, and a dated timeline of events. Organise originals and copies separately. These are routinely required by police, lawyers, tribunals, and courts.

title: Department of Justice — receipt of legal advice
content: The Department of Justice provides public legal education, legal advice services, and referral information, including guidance on where to seek legal assistance. Carry identification and organised documents when seeking advice.

title: Protection from domestic violence
citation: Protection Against Domestic Violence Act, No. 2 of 2015
content: Survivors can apply to court for protection orders including occupation, tenancy, and non-contact orders, and may report to police and access shelters and legal aid. Breach of a protection order is an offence. Keep the court order, OB number, and evidence of any breach.

title: Drink-driving and dangerous driving — general guidance
content: Drink-driving, speeding, and dangerous driving attract fines, licence action, and possible jail terms, and weaken any civil claim. Cooperate with testing when lawfully required and seek a lawyer early. Keep the charge sheet, test records, and hearing dates.

title: Applying for a duplicate logbook — general guidance
content: The registered owner can apply for a duplicate logbook through TIMS where the original is lost, defaced or full, usually with a police abstract and fees. Only the true owner should apply, and buyers should wait for the duplicate before paying in full. Keep the police abstract, application receipts and new logbook copy.

title: Unpaid import duty and motor ownership risk — general guidance
citation: Customs law guidance; Kenya Revenue Authority guidance
content: A vehicle with unpaid duty or disputed customs clearance can be seized even if you bought it innocently. Ask for duty payment proof and verify registration details before paying. Keep duty receipts, import documents and the NTSA search result.

title: Online shopping and deliveries — general guidance
content: For online purchases, screenshot the listing, seller identity, price, and delivery promise, and pay through traceable means. If goods never arrive or differ materially, demand remedy in writing and escalate to the platform, regulator, or small claims with the evidence trail.

title: E-filing and court fees — general guidance
content: Many Kenyan courts use online e-filing with assessed fees payable before processing. Create an account early, scan documents clearly, and keep payment receipts and case numbers. Fee waivers or legal aid may be available for qualifying persons.

title: E-filing on the Judiciary portal — general guidance
content: Many courts require cases to be filed through the judiciary e-filing portal with scanned pleadings and online payment. Litigants receive case numbers and hearing notices electronically. Keep digital receipts and printed copies of e-filed documents.

title: Environment and Land Court — general guidance
citation: Environment and Land Court Act, No. 19 of 2011
content: Land ownership, boundaries, tenancies tied to land, and environmental disputes are heard by the Environment and Land Court. Filing requires title documents, search results, survey reports, and correspondence. Consider mediation where the court offers it.

title: Filing land cases in the ELC — general guidance
content: ELC suits require pleadings, land records, maps and any prior tribunal or chief decisions. The court encourages site visits and settlement where appropriate. Keep certified land searches and filed pleadings together.

title: Environment and Land Court jurisdiction — general guidance
citation: Environment and Land Court Act; Judiciary guidance
content: The Environment and Land Court handles disputes over land ownership, boundaries, leases, planning and environment. It has equal status with the High Court within its subject area. Keep title deeds, survey maps and correspondence about the dispute.

title: ELRC conciliation and hearing steps — general guidance
content: After filing the memorandum of claim, the court may direct conciliation or mention for directions before a full hearing. Evidence includes employment records and witness testimony. Keep conciliation reports and hearing notices filed chronologically.

title: Employment and Labour Relations Court — general guidance
citation: Employment and Labour Relations Court Act; Judiciary guidance
content: The ELRC hears employment, labour and workplace disputes including unfair termination and wage claims. Parties are expected to attempt conciliation through the labour office before filing in many cases. Keep the employment contract, payslips and termination letters.

title: Absconding and desertion allegations
content: Employers alleging desertion must still follow notice and hearing steps and compute dues. Employees delayed by emergency should communicate in writing. Keep messages and medical or incident proof.

title: Affordable Housing Levy on payslips
content: Check that the housing levy on the payslip matches official KRA computation and appears in remittance records. Raise mismatches with payroll in writing. Keep payslips and KRA statements.

title: Annual leave accrual and forfeiture
content: Employees accrue annual leave with pay and unused days have carry-over rules. Refused leave should be documented in writing. Keep leave applications, approvals, and balances on payslips.

title: Nursing breaks after maternity
content: Nursing mothers are entitled to reasonable breaks for breastfeeding on return to work. Agree scheduling in writing with the supervisor. Keep the agreement and any refusal notes.

title: Casual to term conversion rights
content: Casuals working continuously may qualify for conversion to term contracts with written particulars. Track days worked, pay, and supervisors. Raise conversion in writing before disputes arise.

title: Collective bargaining agreements
content: Registered CBAs set binding terms on pay and conditions for covered employees. Request a copy from the union or HR when disputing dues. Keep the CBA extract and payslips.

title: Certificate of service on exit
content: Every employee is entitled to a certificate of service stating the role and duration on termination. Request it in writing if withheld. Keep the certificate for future job applications.

title: Construction site workers: safety and pay
content: Site workers need protective gear, site induction, and documented pay for days worked. Report unsafe sites to DOSH with photos. Keep day-work records and payment messages.

title: Challenging hiring or promotion bias
content: Bias in hiring, pay, or promotion on protected grounds is prohibited. Keep adverts, shortlists, appraisals, and decision letters. Seek internal review, then labour office advice.

title: Rights of domestic workers
content: Domestic workers are employees entitled to contracts, minimum pay, rest, leave, and NSSF/SHIF remittance. Put terms in writing with off days and duties. Keep payment records and communications.

title: Filing a memorandum of claim at ELRC
content: ELRC claims attach the contract, termination letter, demand history, and computation of dues. File within limitation periods. Keep filed pleadings and service proof.

title: Computing terminal dues
content: Final dues combine notice pay, accrued leave, prorated salary, and contractual benefits less lawful deductions. Ask for an itemised statement. Keep payslips and the clearance form.

title: Fixed-term contracts and renewal expectations
content: Fixed-term contracts end on expiry, but repeated renewals can create expectations courts examine. Non-renewal notices should be in writing. Keep all successive contracts and renewal messages.

title: Work permits for foreign employees
content: Foreign workers need the correct permit class applied before reporting, with employer sponsorship. Verify validity rather than holding originals. Keep permit copies and receipts.

title: Reporting sexual harassment at work
content: Employers must have harassment policies and act on complaints. Report in writing to HR or management with dates, messages, and witnesses. Escalate to the labour office or ELRC if ignored.

title: Right to be heard before dismissal
content: Before termination for misconduct or poor performance, the employer must explain the reasons and hear the employee with a companion present. Minutes should be recorded. Keep the invitation, minutes, and outcome letter.

title: Househelp SHIF and NSSF registration
citation: Social Health Insurance Act, 2023; NSSF Act, 2013
content: Employers of domestic workers should register and remit SHIF and NSSF with monthly records. Confirm active cover for hospital visits. Keep registration and remittance receipts.

title: Reporting workplace injury the same day
content: Report injuries to the supervisor immediately, seek treatment, and ensure the employer files with DOSH. Keep treatment notes, incident reports, and witness names for compensation.

title: Interns and attachés: stipends and terms
content: Internships should have written terms on duration, stipend, supervision, and certificates. Unclear terms are clarified before reporting. Keep the offer letter, reports, and stipend records.

title: Jua kali artisan engagements
content: Fundis and workshop hands should agree scope, price, timelines, and materials in writing. Payment disputes rely on messages and delivery proof. Keep quotations and M-Pesa records.

title: Filing at the county labour office
content: Complaints are lodged with contracts, payslips, and a dated statement. Officers attempt conciliation before referral. Keep the complaint number and conciliation notes.

title: Maternity leave and protection
content: Female employees qualify for maternity leave with pay subject to service conditions, and dismissal on pregnancy grounds is prohibited. Notify in writing with expected dates. Keep antenatal records and the leave approval.

title: Dismissal during pregnancy or leave
content: Termination connected to pregnancy or maternity leave is prohibited and actionable. Keep antenatal records, leave approvals, and the dismissal letter for the labour office or ELRC.

title: Minimum wage orders by area and sector
content: Minimum wages vary by urban area and occupation under gazetted orders reviewed periodically. Confirm the current order for the county and job group. Keep payslips and the applicable order printout.

title: Non-compete and confidentiality clauses
citation: Law of Contract Act; Employment Act
content: Restraint clauses must be reasonable in scope and duration to be enforceable. Get advice before signing or breaching. Keep the signed contract and any breach allegations.

title: Notice periods under the Employment Act
content: Notice length follows the contract or the statutory scale based on pay intervals where the contract is silent. Payment in lieu is allowed. Keep the contract, payslips, and termination notice to compute dues.

title: Checking NSSF remittance as an employee
content: Employees can verify NSSF contributions through statements and the fund channels. Report missing remittances first to the employer, then the fund. Keep payslips and fund statements.

title: Overtime pay and working hours
citation: Employment Act, 2007; Regulation of Wages Orders
content: Normal hours and overtime rates follow the Act and wage orders for the sector. Keep rosters, clock records, and payslips showing hours. Claim arrears first in writing to the employer.

title: Paternity leave for fathers
content: Male employees are entitled to paternity leave with pay on the birth of a child. Apply in writing with the expected date and birth notification. Keep the approval and birth records.

title: P9 forms and tax on exit
content: Employers issue P9 forms summarising annual pay and tax for returns and new-employer onboarding. Request the P9 and final payslip on exit. Keep KRA returns and iTax records.

title: Itemised payslips every pay day
content: Employees are entitled to written pay statements showing gross, deductions, and net. Missing payslips weaken loan and dispute claims. Request them monthly and archive copies.

title: Performance improvement plans
content: PIPs should set measurable targets, support, and review dates. Challenge vague or shifting goals in writing. Keep appraisals, targets, and review minutes.

title: Probation periods and confirmation
content: Probation must be agreed in writing with a limited duration and possible extension. Unsatisfactory probation still requires notice and a hearing. Keep the probation clause, appraisals, and confirmation letter.

title: Redundancy notice and severance
content: Redundancies require advance notice to the employee, union, and labour office plus severance computation. Selection criteria must be fair. Keep the redundancy notice, selection records, and payment schedule.

title: Resigning properly and notice
content: Resign in writing with the contractual notice and handover. The employer must settle dues and issue a certificate of service. Keep the resignation acceptance and clearance records.

title: Retirement age and pension processing
content: Retirement follows the contract or scheme rules with notice and benefits processing. Start pension paperwork early with IDs and service records. Keep benefit statements and correspondence.

title: Delivery rider and driver engagements
content: Rider terms should state pay model, fuel, maintenance, and accident cover. Classify correctly as employee or contractor from the facts. Keep trip records and payment statements.

title: Workplace safety committees
content: Larger workplaces must have safety committees and risk assessments. Workers can raise hazards in writing to the committee and DOSH. Keep complaint copies and inspection notes.

title: Delayed salaries: steps to take
content: Demand arrears in writing with months owed and amounts, then escalate to the labour office with payslips and bank statements. Keep the demand letter and delivery proof.

title: Secondment and transfer of employees
content: Secondments should be documented with the host, duration, reporting, and who pays. Refusals of transfer depend on contract mobility clauses. Keep the secondment letter and pay records.

title: Private security guards: hours and pay
citation: Employment Act; Private Security Regulation Act, 2016
content: Guards face long shifts that must still respect hours, overtime, and rest rules, with licensed employers. Keep duty rosters, payslips, and licence details when raising underpayment.

title: Service pay on termination
content: Employees without pension or gratuity coverage may qualify for service pay for completed years. Compute from the contract and payslips. Keep NSSF statements and gratuity records to prove eligibility.

title: Checking SHIF remittance as an employee
content: Employees should confirm SHIF registration and monthly remittance to keep cover active for dependants. Raise gaps with HR, then the fund. Keep registration details and remittance confirmations.

title: Sick leave procedure and certificates
content: Sick leave follows notification and medical certificates for longer absence, with full and half-pay phases. Submit certificates promptly. Keep medical notes and delivery proof.

title: Protected strikes and lock-outs
content: Strikes in essential services and without statutory notice lose protection. Unions must follow dispute and ballot steps. Keep strike notices and conciliator correspondence.

title: Summary dismissal for gross misconduct
content: Summary dismissal without notice is allowed only for gross misconduct such as theft, violence, or wilful neglect, and the employer must still hear the employee. Demand written reasons and keep the dismissal letter for challenge.

title: Board of management teachers contracts
content: BOM teachers should hold written contracts stating pay, subjects, and term. Unpaid arrears are claimed first in writing to the board. Keep contracts, timetables, and payment records.

title: Transfer to another branch or town
content: Transfers depend on mobility clauses and must be communicated with timelines and allowances. Object in writing where hardship or contract breach arises. Keep the transfer letter and contract.

title: Challenging unfair termination
content: Dismissals without valid reason or fair procedure can be challenged at the labour office and the ELRC for reinstatement or compensation. Act within limitation periods. Keep the dismissal letter, contract, and payslips.

title: Joining a trade union
content: Employees may join registered unions of their choice with check-off deductions on written authority. Victimisation for union activity is prohibited. Keep membership cards and deduction records.

title: Volunteers and stipend disputes
content: Volunteer terms should be written with hours, stipend, and duration to avoid later employment claims. Disputes turn on control and pay evidence. Keep the volunteer agreement and records.

title: Answering show-cause and warning letters
content: Respond to show-cause letters factually within the deadline, attaching supporting evidence and witnesses. Keep copies of the letter, response, and delivery proof for the hearing.

title: Work injury compensation claims
content: Compensation covers medical costs and assessed disability following reported workplace injuries. File with medical reports and employer records. Keep DOSH reports and payment decisions.

title: Hiring staff: compliance — general guidance
content: Employers must issue contracts and payslips, remit PAYE, SHIF, and NSSF, and observe safety rules. Non-compliance creates back-payment and penalty risk. Keep payroll, remittance receipts, and employee files.

title: Employee and customer data for businesses — general guidance
content: Businesses holding staff or customer data should limit collection, secure records, and honour access and deletion requests. CCTV and marketing messages need clear notices and opt-outs. Keep consent forms and breach response records.

title: Employment Act, 2007
content: The Employment Act governs terms of employment including contracts, wages, working hours, leave, termination, and remedies. Employers must give written particulars of employment and follow fair procedure before termination. Keep contracts, payslips, warning letters, and termination notices.

title: Employment contracts and casual work — general guidance
content: Employees should have written terms covering job, pay, hours, and leave. Casual workers engaged continuously may qualify for conversion protections. Keep offer letters, timesheets, M-Pesa salary records, and any messages about duties or pay.

title: Workplace discrimination and harassment — general guidance
content: Discrimination and sexual harassment at work are prohibited. Employers should have reporting policies. Keep messages, witness names, incident dates, and copies of complaints made to HR or management for labour office or court referral.

title: Leave entitlements — general guidance
content: Employees accrue rights to annual leave, sick leave, maternity and paternity leave subject to qualifying conditions. Denial of leave or dismissal for pregnancy-related reasons may be challenged. Keep leave applications, approvals, medical notes, and birth records.

title: Payslips and lawful deductions — general guidance
content: Employees in Kenya are entitled to clear payslips showing gross pay, statutory deductions, and other lawful deductions such as approved loans or contributions. Employers should not deduct wages except as allowed by law or written agreement. Keep payslips, contracts, and deduction authorisations.

title: Redundancy — general guidance
content: Redundancy must follow due process including consultation and notice to the labour office and union where applicable. Affected employees may be entitled to severance pay. Keep redundancy notices, selection criteria, and payment records.

title: Workplace safety and injury — general guidance
citation: Occupational Safety and Health Act, No. 15 of 2007; Work Injury Benefits Act, 2007
content: Employers must provide a safe workplace and report serious accidents. Injured employees should seek treatment, report the injury to the employer promptly, and keep medical and DOSH reports for compensation claims under the Work Injury Benefits Act.

title: Terminal dues and clearance on exit — general guidance
content: Employees leaving work in Kenya are generally entitled to settlement of earned wages, accrued leave, notice pay where applicable, and any contractual benefits. Employers commonly use a clearance process for tools, advances, and handover before final payment. Keep payslips, clearance forms, and final payment records.

title: Termination and unfair dismissal — general guidance
content: Employers must give notice or pay in lieu of notice except for gross misconduct, and must follow fair hearing procedure. Unfair or wrongful dismissal can be challenged through the labour office or the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Act quickly and keep the dismissal letter and final dues computation.

title: Wages, overtime and deductions — general guidance
content: Employees are entitled to timely payment of wages, regulated working hours, and regulated deductions. Minimum wages vary by area and sector under wage orders. Keep payslips, bank or M-Pesa statements, and records of hours worked and deductions.

title: Electricity and energy complaints — general guidance
content: Meter, billing, and safety complaints should go to the distributor in writing with meter numbers and photos, then to the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority if unresolved. Keep tokens receipts, bills, and reference numbers.

title: eTIMS invoicing for traders — general guidance
content: Businesses within scope must issue electronic invoices through eTIMS using approved devices or solutions. Exempt and zero-rated supplies must still be correctly categorised on the invoice. Keep eTIMS records reconciled to sales and VAT returns.

title: Eviction process — general guidance
content: Eviction from residential premises generally requires lawful process with proper notice and, where contested, a court or tribunal order. Tenants facing eviction may seek interim relief. The correct process depends on tenancy type, notice given, and reason for eviction.

title: Parental access and visitation schedules
content: Access orders set pickup times, holidays, communication, and handover points. Breaches are enforced back in court. Keep a dated diary of compliance and messages.

title: Adoption through accredited agencies
content: Adoption requires agency assessment, home study, consents, and a court order with amended birth records. Private payment for children is prohibited. Keep agency records and the adoption order.

title: Costs of divorce proceedings
content: Divorce involves filing fees, service costs, and possible advocate fees with fee waivers for qualifying persons. Budget for each stage and ask about legal aid. Keep all payment receipts.

title: Birth registration and certificates
citation: Births and Deaths Registration Act, Cap. 149
content: Register births early with hospital notification and parent IDs for school, travel, and inheritance. Late registration needs additional affidavits. Keep notification slips and receipts.

title: School bullying reports
citation: Basic Education Act, 2013; school safety guidance
content: Report bullying in writing to class teacher and head with dates, messages, and injuries. Escalate to the board and TSC where ignored. Keep medical notes and correspondence.

title: Corporal punishment complaints
content: Caning and degrading punishment in schools are prohibited. Report with medical evidence to the head, TSC, and children officers. Keep treatment notes and witness names.

title: Placing a child in a charitable home
content: Placements go through children officers to registered institutions with case reviews. Families should stay in contact and attend reviews. Keep placement letters and review notes.

title: Resolving custody through elders first
content: Minor custody disagreements can start with chiefs or elders for faster agreement, recorded in writing with witnesses. Serious or violent cases go straight to children officers and courts.

title: Child labour prohibitions
content: Employment of children below the legal minimum age and hazardous work for minors are prohibited. Report to labour officers and children officers with details. Keep birth records and work evidence.

title: Christian marriage registration
content: Church weddings must be conducted by licensed ministers with a marriage book return to the Registrar. Confirm the church licence and return before celebrating. Keep the church certificate and civil certificate.

title: Civil marriage before the Registrar
content: Civil marriages require notice to the Registrar, witnesses, and issuance of a certificate. Book early and carry IDs and passport photos. Keep the notice receipt and certificate.

title: Cohabitation without marriage (come-we-stay)
content: Long cohabitation alone does not automatically equal marriage; presumption depends on conduct such as reputation and children. Protect property with written agreements and joint records. Keep shared bills and contribution proof.

title: Best interests of the child in custody
content: Courts decide custody on safety, care, schooling, health, and the child's views according to age. Interim orders protect schooling during disputes. Keep school, medical, and prior order records.

title: Proving a customary marriage
content: Customary unions need evidence of rites under the community customs plus registration. Elders testimony, dowry records, and ceremony photos help. Register promptly to protect spouses and children.

title: Ending a customary marriage
content: Customary divorce follows the community customs plus formal registration of the dissolution. Return of dowry follows custom and agreement. Record the elders decision in writing.

title: Death certificate for a spouse
citation: Births and Deaths Registration Act, Cap. 149
content: Surviving spouses obtain death certificates with burial permits, IDs, and chief letters for succession and benefits. Apply promptly to unlock claims. Keep multiple certified copies.

title: Support for children with disabilities
citation: Persons with Disabilities Act, 2003; Children Act
content: Children with disabilities are entitled to assessment, reasonable accommodation in school, and registration with the National Council. Keep assessment reports and registration cards for programme access.

title: Filing a divorce petition
content: Divorce petitions attach the marriage certificate, birth certificates of children, property lists, and the reasons with evidence. Service on the spouse follows court rules. Keep filed copies and service affidavits.

title: Grounds for divorce by marriage type
content: Divorce grounds differ: adultery, cruelty, desertion, and irretrievable breakdown apply depending on the marriage system. Petitions need the certificate and evidence. A lawyer confirms the applicable ground.

title: Dowry and bride price records
content: Dowry payments evidence customary marriage negotiations and family consent. Record amounts, dates, witnesses, and outstanding balances. Keep payment notes and elder confirmations.

title: Disputing unlawful school levies
content: Public schools may not impose levies outside approved charges. Raise the fee structure with the head teacher and board, then county education officers. Keep fee structures and payment receipts.

title: Foster care placement
content: Foster placement runs through children officers and approved families with assessments and supervision. Foster parents receive support and monitoring visits. Keep placement records and officer contacts.

title: Safety planning for domestic abuse
content: Plan exit routes, emergency contacts, packed documents, and safe shelter options before leaving. Helplines and rescue centres assist with relocation. Keep copies of IDs and orders with a trusted person.

title: Appointing a guardian for minors
content: Parents travelling or unwell can formalise guardianship through written consent and court orders for school and medical decisions. Informal handover confers no legal authority. Keep consent letters and court orders.

title: GBV helplines and rescue contacts
citation: State Department for Gender; legal aid guidance
content: National helplines, police gender desks, hospitals, and legal aid clinics form the referral chain for survivors. Call first where in danger, then document. Keep helpline reference numbers and referral slips.

title: Hindu marriage requirements
content: Hindu marriages follow Hindu rites with registration under the Act. Keep ceremony evidence and registration for property and travel purposes.

title: Protecting a minor's inheritance
content: Shares for minors are held in trust with court supervision and cannot be sold casually by guardians. Insist on court approval for any dealings. Keep succession orders and trust records.

title: Islamic marriage and Kadhi registration
content: Islamic marriages are celebrated under Islamic rites and registered with a Kadhi or licensed Imam. The mahr terms should be recorded. Keep the Kadhi certificate and IDs.

title: Maintenance in Kadhi courts
content: Muslim spouses may seek maintenance and custody orders in Kadhi courts applying Islamic law within constitutional limits. Keep marriage records, birth certificates, and expense proof.

title: How child maintenance is assessed
content: Courts weigh each parent's means against school fees, rent share, food, medical, and transport. Prepare budgets with receipts. Keep fee structures, receipts, and income evidence.

title: Varying maintenance when income changes
content: Job loss or new needs justify variation applications with fresh income and expense proof. Do not stop paying unilaterally. Keep the original order and new evidence.

title: The five systems of marriage
content: Five marriage systems operate in Kenya — civil, customary, Christian, Hindu, and Islamic — each with distinct celebration and registration rules. Unregistered unions are hard to prove in succession and property disputes. Keep the certificate and ceremony records.

title: Protecting the matrimonial home
content: Neither spouse should sell or charge the matrimonial home without the other's consent during marriage. Caveats and court orders can block disposal. Keep title copies and consent records.

title: Mediation before contested divorce
content: Courts encourage mediation on custody, maintenance, and property to save time and cost. Settlements are recorded as consent orders. Keep mediation referrals and agreements.

title: Changing a child's name
citation: Registration of Documents; civil registration guidance
content: Name changes run through deed poll and gazette processes with parental consent and birth record updates. Both parents should consent in writing. Keep the deed, gazette notice, and new records.

title: Reporting child neglect by a parent
content: Report sustained neglect to children officers and chiefs with feeding, school, and medical evidence. Officers assess and may place the child safely. Keep dated notes and witness details.

title: Passport for a minor
content: Minor passports need birth certificates, parental IDs, and consent of both parents or court order. Apply through eCitizen with an appointment. Keep application references and receipts.

title: Disputed paternity and DNA tests
content: Courts can order DNA testing where paternity is disputed for maintenance or custody. Testing follows chain-of-custody at accredited labs. Keep court orders and lab receipts.

title: Polygamous and potentially polygamous marriages
content: Customary and Islamic marriages may be polygamous while civil, Christian, and Hindu marriages are monogamous. Converting between systems has consent rules. Keep certificates for each union.

title: Dividing matrimonial property
content: Division follows proven monetary and non-monetary contribution, not automatic halves. Gather title deeds, loan statements, and domestic-contribution evidence. Keep receipts for improvements.

title: Challenging school exclusion or expulsion
content: Exclusions must follow disciplinary procedure with parental hearing. Appeal to the board and county education office with records. Keep suspension letters, hearing minutes, and fee receipts.

title: Transferring schools mid-year
content: Mid-year transfers need clearance, assessment records, and NEMIS updates between schools. Request transfer letters early. Keep report forms and clearance slips.

title: Separation agreements before divorce
content: Couples may separate by written agreement covering residence, children, maintenance, and property while deciding next steps. Have it witnessed and keep copies. Unsafe situations should prioritise protection orders.

title: Spousal maintenance after separation
content: Courts may order interim support considering needs and means during divorce. Prepare budgets and income proof. Keep the application, order, and payment records.

title: Surname change after marriage
content: Name use after marriage follows ID updates with the marriage certificate through civil registration. Update KRA, bank, and employer records consistently. Keep the certificate and update receipts.

title: Teen pregnancy: school re-entry
citation: Basic Education Act; school re-entry guidelines
content: Pregnant learners and young mothers have the right to continue schooling with re-entry support. Engage the head teacher and guidance office early. Keep antenatal and re-admission records.

title: Travel consent for minors
content: Travel with minors, especially abroad, needs birth certificates and the other parent's written consent or court order. Airlines and immigration check these. Keep consent letters and court orders.

title: Rights of widows and widowers
citation: Law of Succession Act; Marriage Act
content: Surviving spouses have inheritance and matrimonial property rights that relatives must respect. Eviction from the matrimonial home is unlawful without court process. Keep marriage and death certificates.

title: Wills for married couples with children
content: Spouses with children should each make wills naming guardians and trustees for minors. Store originals safely and tell executors. Keep copies with the marriage certificate.

title: Adoption process and consent — general guidance
content: Adoption in Kenya is a court process supervised through accredited agencies and children officers, with consent, background checks, and the best interests of the child at its centre. Adoptive parents receive a court order and amended birth records after successful placement. Keep agency records, consents, and the adoption order.

title: Customary marriage requirements — general guidance
content: Customary marriages in Kenya arise under the customs of the parties and must be registered to be easily proved for inheritance, property, and children matters. Families should record dowry, consent, and ceremony details according to their community customs. Keep the marriage certificate and any customary ceremony records.

title: Protection against FGM and early marriage — general guidance
citation: Prohibition of Female Genital Mutilation Act; Children Act, 2022
content: Female genital mutilation and marriage of children are prohibited in Kenya, and suspected cases can be reported to police, chiefs, children officers, or helplines. Survivors can access medical care, counselling, and protective court orders. Keep medical reports and any incident or OB records safely.

title: Guardianship and custody of children — general guidance
content: Courts in Kenya decide custody, access, and guardianship based on the best interests of the child, considering safety, care, schooling, and the child's views. Parents and relatives can seek interim orders where a child is at risk or schooling is disrupted. Keep birth certificates, school records, and any prior orders.

title: Islamic marriage registration — general guidance
content: Islamic marriages in Kenya are celebrated according to Islamic rites and should be registered with a licensed Kadhi, Imam, or registrar. Registration helps prove the marriage for maintenance, custody, succession, and travel documents. Keep the marriage certificate and identification documents.

title: Divorce and Kadhi courts for Muslim families — general guidance
content: Muslim spouses in Kenya may seek dissolution and related custody and maintenance orders through the Kadhi courts where the parties profess Islam. The court considers Islamic law alongside the welfare of children and procedural fairness. Keep marriage records, birth certificates, and court orders.

title: Enforcing child maintenance orders — general guidance
content: Where a parent defaults on court-ordered child maintenance, the other parent can return to court for enforcement through attachment, arrears, or other lawful measures. Courts can review the amount where income or needs have materially changed. Keep the court order, payment records, and proof of the child's expenses.

title: Domestic violence — general guidance
content: Survivors of domestic violence can seek protection orders, report to police, and access shelters and legal aid. Urgent safety planning and medical care should be prioritised. Keep P3 forms, photos, messages, and witness contacts.

title: Parental responsibility for unmarried parents — general guidance
content: Both parents share responsibility for children, and unmarried fathers may acquire parental responsibility through agreement, registration, or court order. Maintenance duty applies regardless of marital status. Keep paternity acknowledgements, support records, and court filings.

title: Buying a motor vehicle still under bank finance — general guidance
citation: General lending guidance; Traffic Act, Cap. 403
content: If the seller is still paying a bank loan, agree in writing how the loan will be cleared and when transfer will happen. Ideally settle the lender directly and obtain a release before paying the seller the balance. Keep the loan statement, settlement letter and payment proofs.

title: Food safety complaints — general guidance
citation: Food, Drugs and Chemical Substances Act, Cap. 254
content: Suspected contaminated food or drink should be reported to public health with the outlet name, receipt, and samples where safe. Seek medical care and keep treatment records for any compensation or enforcement follow-up.

title: Forged or altered logbooks — general guidance
content: Forgery can involve altered names, engine numbers or fake logbook printouts, so compare the physical vehicle markings with TIMS records. Be wary of deals where the seller cannot log into TIMS or show original documents. Keep copies of documents offered and the official search outcome.

title: Fraud and obtaining by false pretences — general guidance
content: Fraud, obtaining money by false pretences, and forgery are criminal offences. Preserve M-Pesa messages, bank statements, contracts, IDs used, and call records, and report promptly to police and, for online cases, the DCI. Do not send more money to recover the loss without advice.

title: Gender-based violence reporting — general guidance
content: Survivors of gender-based violence should prioritise safety and medical care, then report to police and request a P3 form and referral to legal aid and psychosocial support. Keep medical records, torn clothing as evidence where advised, messages, and witness details. The National Legal Aid Service line is 0800 720 640.

title: GBV shelters and helplines — general guidance
citation: State Department for Gender; legal aid guidance
content: GBV survivors can access rescue centres, toll-free helplines, and legal aid clinics in addition to police and hospitals. If in immediate danger, move to safety and call for help first, then document injuries and preserve messages for reporting.

title: Affidavits for lost documents
content: Swear loss affidavits with document details, OB numbers where applicable, and commissioner stamps for replacements. Keep commissioned copies.

title: Late birth registration
content: Late registration needs clinic cards, affidavits, and chief letters with fees. Start early for school and IDs. Keep notification slips.

title: Certifying documents
content: Certify copies with commissioners or issuing offices for filings. Keep certification receipts with the bundle.

title: When offices ask for chief letters
content: Chiefs confirm residence, family, and events with IDs and witnesses. Attend with documents and neighbours where needed. Keep stamped copies.

title: Reporting dead livestock or disease
content: Report sudden deaths to veterinary officers without moving carcasses. Keep treatment and vaccination records.

title: Disability registration and card
content: Assess at county hospitals, then register with the National Council for services and tax considerations. Keep assessment reports and the card.

title: Building a case file that wins
content: Keep IDs, contracts, receipts, messages, photos, and reference numbers in one dated file with originals separate. Organised files get faster help at every office. Update the timeline after each event.

title: Setting up eCitizen correctly
content: Register with your ID, verified phone, and email with strong passwords. Link KRA, NTSA, and BRS services. Keep login recovery details safe.

title: FIDA-Kenya for women and children
content: FIDA supports women and children on family, GBV, and succession matters through clinics and representation. Carry IDs and case documents. Keep intake references.

title: Filing nil and normal returns
content: File income returns yearly even where income is nil to avoid penalties, with P9 and business records. Keep filing receipts.

title: Help after fires
content: Report to fire services, police, and chiefs with loss lists for relief and investigations. Keep OB, photos, and assistance records.

title: First aid after injuries
content: Stop bleeding, call emergency services, and preserve the scene for investigators. Keep treatment records for claims.

title: Help after floods and disasters
content: Report to chiefs and Red Cross with damage photos for relief and assessment. Keep loss lists and assistance records.

title: Reporting illegal dumping
content: Report dumping with photos and locations to county environment and NEMA. Use licensed collectors. Keep receipts and references.

title: Police clearance for jobs
content: Apply on eCitizen with fingerprints at gazetted centres for job and travel clearance. Keep the payment receipt and certificate.

title: University funding model appeals
content: Appeal banding with household and admission evidence within timelines. Meet documentation checklists. Keep award and appeal records.

title: Kituo cha Sheria legal aid
content: Kituo offers legal aid on evictions, employment, and criminal matters through offices and clinics. Book with documents ready. Keep appointment records.

title: New electricity connections
content: Apply with IDs, plot, and wiring certificates, paying official fees. Avoid middlemen. Keep application and payment records.

title: Getting a KRA PIN
content: Apply on iTax with ID and details, then collect the PIN certificate. Update details on changes. Keep the certificate secure.

title: Paying land rates and rent
content: Pay county rates and national ground rent before penalties block transfers. Keep demand notes and clearance receipts.

title: Getting counselling help
content: Reach counsellors, helplines, and clinics early; emergencies go to hospitals. Helplines include 1199 and 0800 720 640 referrals. Keep referral records.

title: Preserving chats and messages
content: Export full chats with dates, back up media, and avoid edits. Screenshots supplement but exports prove context. Keep originals and exports.

title: Separate meters in rentals
content: Agree meter separation costs and billing in writing with the landlord before splitting. Keep agreements and installer receipts.

title: Getting help from NLAS
content: Apply at NLAS centres with IDs, case documents, and income proof; the toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Follow up with the file reference. Keep the reference and appointment slips.

title: Reporting noise pollution
content: Log dates and times with recordings, then report to NEMA, county, or police. Night violations attract enforcement. Keep the diary and references.

title: NSSF self-registration
content: Self-employed persons register with ID and contribute monthly for benefits. Keep the member number and payment records.

title: Cash transfers for older persons
content: Enroll through social development officers with IDs for Inua Jamii consideration. Report payment failures with records. Keep enrollment slips.

title: Originals vs copies
content: Courts prefer originals; keep them safe and file certified copies where required. Never alter originals. Keep a copy log.

title: Support for orphans and vulnerable children
content: Report to children officers for placement, schooling, and cash-transfer consideration with birth and death records. Keep officer contacts and records.

title: Applying for a passport
content: Apply on eCitizen with birth certificate, IDs, photos, and recommender details. Book biometrics. Keep application references.

title: Storing fuel at home safely
content: Avoid storing petrol indoors; use approved containers away from flames. Report illegal dens. Keep purchase receipts from licensed stations.

title: Photos that count as evidence
content: Take wide, medium, and close shots with dates, locations, and intact metadata. Back up originals. Keep printed and digital sets.

title: Getting a police abstract
content: Apply at the reporting station with the OB number and IDs, pay the fee, and collect the signed abstract. Keep the abstract for insurers and registries.

title: Prepaid water meters
content: Top up through official channels with meter numbers and keep tokens. Dispute faulty deductions with readings. Keep token records.

title: Pro bono and university law clinics
citation: Legal aid and clinical education guidance
content: Law school clinics and LSK pro bono schemes assist qualifying matters with documents and merit screening. Apply with the full file. Keep referral letters.

title: Bursaries and CDF applications
content: Apply with fee structures, results, and chief letters before deadlines at ward offices. Keep application receipts and award letters.

title: Registering for SHIF (SHA)
content: Register households with IDs and dependants through SHA channels and confirm facility empanelment. Keep registration and contribution records.

title: Tax compliance certificates
content: Clear returns and debts before applying for TCC needed for tenders and jobs. Keep the certificate and renewal dates.

title: Writing a clear incident timeline
content: List dates, places, people, and what happened in order with supporting documents per entry. Timelines expose gaps and deadlines. Keep the timeline updated.

title: Translating documents for filings
content: Translate foreign-language documents with certified translators for court and registry use. Keep translator certificates.

title: Tree planting and chief permits
content: Source seedlings from licensed nurseries and confirm planting sites with chiefs where public land is used. Keep seedling receipts.

title: New water connections
content: Apply to the county provider with IDs and plot details, pay connection fees officially. Keep application and payment records.

title: Recording witness details early
content: Note names, contacts, and what each witness saw with dates. Memories fade fast. Keep the list with the timeline.

title: Basic education rights and school fees — general guidance
content: Every child in Kenya has a right to free and compulsory basic education, and public schools should not impose unlawful levies beyond approved charges. Parents facing exclusion over fees or uniforms can escalate to head teachers, boards, and county education officers. Keep fee structures, receipts, and admission records.

title: Citizenship, IDs and passports — general guidance
content: Kenyan citizenship by birth, registration, or naturalisation supports access to IDs, passports, and other civil documents through immigration and civil registration offices. Applicants should use official eCitizen channels and carry original supporting documents. Keep application references, receipts, and birth records.

title: Rights of persons with disabilities — general guidance
content: Persons with disabilities in Kenya are entitled to dignity, access, reasonable accommodation, and protection from discrimination in work, school, and services. Registration with the National Council for Persons with Disabilities supports access to programmes and tax considerations. Keep assessment reports, registration cards, and correspondence.

title: Medical negligence complaints — general guidance
citation: Health Act, 2017; Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Council Act
content: Patients who suffer harm from suspected negligent care in Kenya can complain to the facility, the Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Council, or other professional boards. Clear treatment records and timelines are important for review and redress. Keep discharge summaries, receipts, prescriptions, and test results.

title: HELB loans and student funding appeals — general guidance
content: Students in Kenyan universities and colleges can apply for HELB loans and scholarships under the prevailing funding model and appeal where allocations seem incorrect. Applicants should meet deadlines and provide accurate household and admission details. Keep application records, award letters, and disbursement statements.

title: NEMA approvals and environmental impact assessment — general guidance
content: Projects likely to affect the environment in Kenya, such as factories, quarries, and large developments, generally require NEMA approval and sometimes a full environmental impact assessment. Affected neighbours can participate during public consultation and raise objections. Keep project notices, submissions, and NEMA correspondence.

title: Noise pollution complaints — general guidance
content: Excessive noise from bars, churches, construction, or events can be reported to NEMA, county environment officers, or police, especially at night. Complainants should record dates, times, and the source to support enforcement. Keep a noise diary and any reports or reference numbers.

title: Protection and support for older persons — general guidance
content: Older persons in Kenya facing neglect, abuse, or property exploitation can seek help from chiefs, social development officers, and police alongside available cash transfer programmes. Families should arrange care, medical support, and safe handling of pensions and property. Keep medical records, payment records, and report references.

title: SHIF registration and health coverage — general guidance
content: The Social Health Insurance Fund has replaced NHIF as Kenya's public health cover, with registration and means-tested contributions for households. Members should confirm registration, dependants, and facility empanelment before seeking care. Keep registration details, contribution receipts, and hospital invoices.

title: Solid waste and dumping complaints — general guidance
citation: Environmental Management and Co-ordination Act, 1999; County by-laws
content: Illegal dumping, burning of waste, and discharge of effluent can be reported to county public health officers and NEMA for enforcement. Households and businesses should use licensed collectors and keep premises clean. Keep photos, collection receipts, and complaint reference numbers.

title: Water use rights and permits — general guidance
content: Abstraction of water from rivers, lakes, or boreholes in Kenya generally requires authorisation from the Water Resources Authority alongside any county service connection. Illegal connections, pollution of water sources, and interference with meters can attract penalties. Keep permits, bills, and payment receipts.

title: Work permits and refugee protection — general guidance
citation: Kenya Citizenship and Immigration Act, 2011; Refugees Act, 2021
content: Foreign nationals working in Kenya generally need the correct class of work permit, while asylum seekers and refugees register with the Department of Refugee Services for protection documents. Employers and landlords should verify valid permits rather than retain originals. Keep permit copies, receipts, and appointment slips.

title: Guarantors and co-signing — general guidance
content: A written guarantee can make you liable for another person's loan, including auction of charged security. Read the guarantee, confirm the cap and notice terms, and keep copies of everything signed plus demand letters received.

title: Hearing evidence and witnesses — general guidance
content: Hearings involve witness testimony, cross-examination and production of documents and exhibits. Parties should bring originals and copies of their evidence bundle. Keep witness statements and exhibit markers organised.

title: Hire purchase for business assets — general guidance
content: Hire purchase lets a business use equipment or vehicles while paying instalments, with ownership passing after the final payment. The agreement must state cash price, hire-purchase price, instalments and repossession terms. Keep the agreement, payment receipts and registration documents together.

title: Hire-purchase for motor vehicles — general guidance
content: Under hire-purchase you use the vehicle while paying instalments but ownership passes only after the final payment and transfer. The agreement should state the cash price, deposit, instalments, total cost, repossession terms and early settlement rights. Keep the signed agreement, payment schedule and all instalment receipts.

title: Hiring staff and written particulars — general guidance
content: Employees engaged for more than a short period should receive written particulars of wages, hours, leave and termination terms. Employers must keep employment records and statutory returns. Keep signed contracts and payroll records for inspections and disputes.

title: Hit-and-run — general guidance
content: Leaving the scene of an accident is a serious offence. Victims should get medical care, report immediately, and preserve any dashcam, CCTV, plate fragments, and witness details. Do not chase dangerously; let police investigate.

title: Agent and viewing fees
content: Confirm agency registration and fee terms before paying viewing or agency fees, and receipt every payment. Fake agents vanish after deposits. Keep listings, IDs, and payment proof.

title: Bedsitter deposits and viewing scams
content: View bedsitters physically, verify the agent, and receipt deposits to the landlord account. Avoid pay-before-view demands. Keep listings and payment proof.

title: Shop tenants and goodwill protection
citation: Landlord and Tenant (Shops, Hotels) Act, Cap. 301
content: Protected shop tenancies have termination and rent safeguards with tribunal recourse. Notices must follow statutory form. Keep the lease, notices, and tribunal filings.

title: Caretaker harassment and demands
content: Caretakers cannot levy new charges, lock gates, or disconnect services without landlord authority and law. Escalate in writing to the landlord or agent. Keep demands, receipts, and messages.

title: Controlled tenancies and fair rent
content: Older low-rent tenancies may be controlled with regulated rents and tribunal oversight. Check control status before agreeing increases. Keep the letting history and tribunal orders.

title: Rent deposits and deductions
content: Deposits are security against arrears and damage, refundable with an itemised statement. Challenge unfair deductions in writing with photos. Keep receipts and the refund statement.

title: Distress for rent: landlord limits
content: Attachment of tenant goods for arrears follows strict legal procedure with inventory and timelines. Irregular distress is challengeable. Keep the distress notice and goods list.

title: Double letting of the same house
content: Where two tenants hold receipts for one house, the earlier verifiable agreement and landlord authority decide. Report fraud to police. Keep agreements, receipts, and messages.

title: Ending a lease early
content: Early exit follows the break clause with notice and handover; otherwise negotiate surrender in writing. Document the meter and key return. Keep the surrender agreement.

title: Defending an eviction suit
content: File a defence with payment records and notice defects before the deadline and attend mentions. Seek interim stay where lockout threatens. Keep pleadings and hearing notices.

title: Fire safety in flats
content: Estates need extinguishers, clear exits, and assembly points with landlord maintenance. Report blocked exits to management and county fire. Keep complaint records and photos.

title: Flooded rental houses
content: Document flooding with photos, notify the landlord in writing, and seek rent relief or relocation where uninhabitable. Report drainage failures to the county. Keep reports and expense receipts.

title: Gated estate monthly dues
content: Estate dues fund security, garbage, and common repairs with budgets approved at meetings. Ask for accounts where dues jump. Keep demand notes and meeting minutes.

title: Guarantors for rent
content: Rent guarantees should cap liability and notice terms in writing. Guarantors get copies of demands. Keep the guarantee and payment records.

title: Hostel and bedsitter rules
content: Hostel terms should state curfews, visitors, deposits, and notice in writing. Safety and sanitation complaints go to management and public health. Keep the admission agreement and receipts.

title: Move-in inventory and photos
content: Record meter readings, defects, and furniture condition with dated photos signed by both sides. This decides deposit deductions later. Keep the inventory with the agreement.

title: Common cleaning and garbage fees
content: Garbage and cleaning levies should be receipted with licensed collection. Report dumping to public health with photos. Keep payment receipts.

title: Key handover and final meter readings
content: Return all keys with a signed handover recording meters, condition, and date. Settle final bills the same day. Keep the handover note and clearance.

title: Legal aid for eviction threats
content: Tenants facing lockout or demolition threats can seek NLAS help with agreements, receipts, and notices. The toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Keep the full tenancy file.

title: Lift breakdowns and service charges
content: Lift maintenance is a service-charge item with inspection duties. Demand maintenance logs where breakdowns recur. Keep demands and incident notes.

title: Lockouts are unlawful without court process
content: Locking out, removing doors, or cutting water or power to force exit is unlawful. Report to police and seek urgent court restoration orders. Keep photos, witness contacts, and utility records.

title: Live-in househelp accommodation
content: Househelp quarters should be habitable with clear work hours separate from tenancy. Put accommodation terms in the employment contract. Keep payment and housing records.

title: Institutional and police housing
content: Service quarters follow institutional allocation rules with deduction and vacation procedures. Keep allocation letters and payslip deductions.

title: Mould and damp health complaints
content: Persistent damp causing illness is reported with medical notes to the landlord and public health. Request relocation or remediation in writing. Keep photos and treatment records.

title: Notice checklist when moving out
content: Give written notice, clear bills, repair damage, photograph the unit, and hand over keys with a signed note. Claim the deposit with the file. Keep every document.

title: Noisy neighbours and landlords duty
content: Report persistent noise with a dated diary to the landlord, agent, and then NEMA or police. Keep recordings, diary entries, and complaint references.

title: Notice to quit: length and form
citation: Rent Restriction Act, Cap. 296; tenancy terms
content: Termination notices must follow the agreement and applicable law in writing with clear dates. Defective notices can be challenged. Keep the notice and proof of delivery.

title: Fair wear and tear vs damage
content: Faded paint and minor scuffs are usually wear, while holes and burns are damage. Compare move-in and move-out photos. Keep both photo sets.

title: Repainting and improvements by tenants
content: Agree improvements and repainting in writing with who pays and reinstatement duties. Unapproved alterations invite deposit deductions. Keep approvals and cost receipts.

title: Pets in rental flats
content: Pets depend on the agreement and estate rules with liability for damage and nuisance on the keeper. Seek written consent. Keep consent and vaccination records.

title: Plot caretaker rent collection
content: Pay caretakers only with landlord-authorised receipts naming the plot and house. Confirm remittance with the landlord periodically. Keep every receipt.

title: Electricity disconnection in rentals
content: Power disconnections follow Kenya Power procedure with bills and notice. Landlords cutting supply to evict act unlawfully. Keep meter numbers, bills, and reconnection records.

title: Rent receipts every payment
content: Insist on receipts or M-Pesa records naming the house, month, and recipient for every payment. Cash without receipt is unprovable. Keep a full payment file.

title: Clearing rent arrears by plan
content: Propose a written catch-up plan with dates and amounts before arrears grow, and honour it. Keep the plan, payments, and landlord acknowledgements.

title: Rent books and payment ledgers
content: Maintain a rent book signed by both sides or a digital ledger reconciled to M-Pesa. Disputes turn on this record. Keep the book and statements together.

title: Challenging unfair rent increases
content: Increases must follow the agreement and law with written notice. Disputes go to negotiation, tribunal, or court with payment history. Keep the agreement and increase notices.

title: Filing at the Rent Tribunal
content: File with the agreement, receipts, notices, and a statement of the dispute on prescribed forms. Attend mentions with originals. Keep filing receipts and orders.

title: Leaking roofs and damp houses
content: Report leaks in writing with dated photos and allow reasonable repair time, then escalate to public health for uninhabitable conditions. Keep repair requests and health reports.

title: Rent deductions from salary
content: Employer-housing deductions need written authorisation within lawful deduction limits. Confirm balances on payslips monthly. Keep authorisation and payslips.

title: Renting near schools: term timing
content: Align lease start with school terms and confirm commute and water reliability before paying. Keep the agreement and school admission records.

title: Break-ins and landlord security duties
content: Report break-ins to police and the landlord with OB numbers, and demand gate, lighting, and lock fixes in writing. Keep OB slips and repair requests.

title: Sewage bursts and sanitation failures
content: Sewage overflows are public health hazards reported to the landlord and public health officers with photos. Seek alternative arrangement where uninhabitable. Keep reports and medical notes.

title: Short-term lets and estate consent
content: Estates may regulate Airbnb-style lets with registration and conduct rules. Confirm management consent before listing. Keep consent, bookings, and guest records.

title: Subletting and Airbnb without consent
content: Subletting against the agreement can ground termination. Seek written landlord consent with terms. Keep consent letters and sub-tenant records.

title: Written tenancy agreements
content: Put rent, deposit, duration, notice, utilities, and repair duties in a signed agreement with inventory. Oral terms are hard to prove. Keep the signed copy and handover photos.

title: Water disconnection in rentals
content: Water cuts for arrears follow provider procedure with notice; landlords must not cut supply as eviction pressure. Pay through official channels. Keep bills, notices, and payment proof.

title: Borehole and vendor water in flats
content: Vendor and borehole water should meet safety standards with treatment records. Report discoloured or unsafe supply to public health. Keep bills and test reports.

title: Caretaker and agent disputes in rental buildings — general guidance
content: Caretakers and agents act for the landlord and generally cannot increase rent, lock out tenants, or disconnect utilities without lawful authority. Tenants with complaints should raise them in writing to the landlord or agent before approaching the Rent Tribunal. Keep rent receipts, notices, and written complaints.

title: Service charge in flats and gated estates — general guidance
content: Service charge covers shared services such as security, cleaning, water, lifts, and common repairs in flats and gated estates. Occupants can ask for budgets, audited accounts, and receipts where charges seem unclear or excessive. Keep demand notes, receipts, and management meeting records.

title: Short-term lets and furnished apartments — general guidance
citation: Rent Restriction Act, Cap. 296; County by-laws
content: Short-term and holiday lets in Kenya are generally governed by the booking contract plus applicable county licensing and estate rules. Guests and hosts should agree in writing on price, house rules, deposits, and liability for damage. Keep booking confirmations, payment records, and photos of the unit condition.

title: Tenant rights — general guidance
citation: Landlord and Tenant (Shops, Hotels and Catering Establishments) Act, Cap. 301
content: Tenants have rights to quiet enjoyment and lawful process before eviction. Commercial premises in the protected category have additional tribunal protections. Keep the tenancy agreement, rent and deposit receipts, and all notices.

title: Phone theft and IMEI blocking — general guidance
citation: Kenya Information and Communications Act; CA guidance
content: After phone theft, report to police with the IMEI, notify the provider to block the SIM, and request device blocking where available. Keep purchase receipts, box IMEI, and police abstract for insurance or recovery.

title: Buying an imported used motor vehicle — general guidance
citation: Kenya Revenue Authority guidance; NTSA guidance
content: Imported vehicles should have proper import documents, duty payment evidence and NTSA registration records. Confirm year of manufacture, mileage history and compliance with Kenya's age and standards rules for imports. Keep import entries, duty receipts, inspection certificates and TIMS records.

title: Injury compensation after accidents — general guidance
content: Injury claims need medical reports, P3 forms, expense receipts, proof of lost income, and the police abstract. Limitation periods apply, so start early and verify deadlines with a lawyer. Keep a dated file of every bill and appointment.

title: Insolvency and bankruptcy — general guidance
content: Individuals and businesses unable to pay debts may explore negotiation, administration, or bankruptcy procedures with serious long-term consequences. Get advice before signing anything, and keep a full list of creditors, amounts, and security held.

title: Insolvency options for struggling businesses — general guidance
content: The Insolvency Act provides administration, company voluntary arrangements and liquidation for companies unable to pay debts. Early advice helps directors choose rescue over closure and understand liability risks. Keep management accounts, creditor lists and board resolutions for the insolvency practitioner.

title: NTSA inspection and vehicle condition — general guidance
content: Vehicles must be roadworthy, and inspection records can reveal condition and compliance issues. Ask when the vehicle was last inspected and whether any defects were noted. Keep inspection reports and repair receipts.

title: Motor insurance claims — general guidance
content: Notify your insurer quickly after an accident with the police abstract, photos, repair estimates, and medical reports. Third-party injury claims follow statutory procedures with strict evidence needs. Keep claim numbers and every submission receipt.

title: Actor and crew contracts
content: Production contracts state roles, pay, hours, image rights, and credit. Pay per milestones. Keep signed contracts and call sheets.

title: Selling art through galleries
content: Gallery consignments state commission, insurance, and return with inventory. Photograph works on handover. Keep agreements and inventory.

title: Selling beats exclusively vs non-exclusively
content: Exclusive sales transfer defined rights to one artist; leases allow reuse. Put scope, term, credit, and royalties in writing. Keep licences and payment proof.

title: Beat stolen from YouTube: evidence pack
content: Assemble project files, dated exports, upload logs, messages, and splits before filing takedowns. Preserve message originals. Keep the evidence bundle with dates.

title: Someone copying your brand
content: Collect purchase evidence, report to ACA and KIPI, and send demands before suing. Keep samples, receipts, and registration certificates.

title: Church use of copyrighted music
content: Churches playing or streaming copyrighted music need blanket licences from CMOs. Obtain licences before events. Keep licences and setlists.

title: How long copyright lasts
content: Copyright generally lasts for the author's life plus a statutory period, differing for sound recordings and broadcasts. Confirm the term for the work type. Keep creation and publication records.

title: Answering a counter-notice
content: Counter-notices assert licence or fair use with evidence and consent to process. Respond within deadlines with counsel. Keep licences and correspondence.

title: Cover songs and remixes
content: Covers and remixes need permission from rights holders except as fair dealing allows. Get licences before release. Keep permission letters and licences.

title: Exporting crafts and curios
content: Craft exports need business records, authorised materials, and customs declarations. CITES permits apply to restricted materials. Keep permits and shipping records.

title: Demand letters for infringement
content: Demands identify the work, the infringement, and the remedy with a deadline before suit. Send with evidence annexed. Keep delivery proof and responses.

title: Industrial designs for product look
content: Product shapes and patterns register as industrial designs with novelty requirements. Keep dated drawings and application records.

title: Distributing music on streaming platforms
content: Distributors need accurate splits, ISRC codes, and rights confirmation before release. Verify royalty statements quarterly. Keep distribution contracts and statements.

title: DJ mixtapes and club sets
content: Mixtapes with others tracks need licences for commercial release; venues carry performance licences. Keep licences and tracklists.

title: Domain names and business names
content: Register matching domains early with verified registrars and renew before expiry. Disputes follow registrar policy. Keep registration and renewal records.

title: IP enforcement: demand, KECOBO and courts — general guidance
content: IP disputes often start with a written demand and negotiation, then KECOBO complaints or mediation, then court action for injunctions, damages, or account of profits. Limitation and evidence rules apply, so act early and preserve originals, registrations, and infringement captures with dates.

title: Fair dealing exceptions
content: Research, private study, criticism, and news reporting may use excerpts with attribution within fair limits. Commercial copying rarely qualifies. Get advice before relying on it.

title: Filming permits and locations
citation: Films and Stage Plays Act; KFCB guidance
content: Commercial shoots need KFCB and county permits with location consent. Apply early with scripts and crew lists. Keep permits and consent letters.

title: Franchise agreements
content: Franchises license brands and systems with fees, territories, training, and audit rights. Verify the franchisor record. Keep the agreement and payment records.

title: Freelance creative contracts
content: Freelance briefs state scope, revisions, timelines, fees, and rights transfer with deposits. Keep briefs, drafts, and payment records.

title: KAMP for producers of sound recordings
content: Producers register recordings with KAMP for neighbouring rights collection. Keep master files and registration records.

title: Complaining to KECOBO
content: Complaints attach registration, infringement captures with dates, and demand history. KECOBO may mediate or refer for prosecution. Keep the complaint reference.

title: KFCB classification of films
content: Films for public exhibition need KFCB examination and rating with submission fees. Keep submission receipts and certificates.
