title: Legal aid for creators
content: Exploited creators can seek NLAS and KECOBO help with contracts, splits, and registrations. The toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Keep all creative records.

title: Logo design ownership
content: Logos transfer only with written assignment; designers retain rights otherwise. Clients secure source files and assignment. Keep design contracts and assignments.

title: MCSK membership for composers
content: Composers and authors join MCSK with IDs, works lists, and fees for royalty collection. Keep membership cards and work declarations.

title: Clearing artist and song names
content: Search KIPI, streaming, and socials for conflicting artist and title names before release. Adjust early. Keep search screenshots.

title: NDAs with staff and partners
content: NDAs define confidential information, duration, and remedies with signatures before disclosure. Keep signed copies and disclosure logs.

title: Using works of unknown owners
content: Document diligent searches for owners before using orphan works, and stop on objection. Keep search records and use logs.

title: Patentability requirements
content: Patents need novelty, inventive step, and industrial application with full disclosure. Public disclosure before filing destroys novelty. Keep lab books confidential.

title: Photography copyright and client use
content: Photographers own images unless assigned in writing; clients get the licensed uses stated. Put deliverables, revisions, and usage in the contract. Keep RAW files and contracts.

title: Book plagiarism and publishing contracts
content: Publishing contracts state royalties, territories, and reversion with manuscript delivery. Register the work with KECOBO. Keep contracts and royalty statements.

title: Poetry and spoken word rights
content: Poems are protected on creation; performances need venue licences and recording consent. Register collections with KECOBO. Keep manuscripts and event records.

title: PRISK for performers
content: Performers register performances with PRISK for broadcast and public-performance royalties. Keep performance records and membership details.

title: Music publishing deals
content: Publishing deals assign administration with advances, splits, and reversion. Compare with CMO collection. Keep deal memos and statements.

title: Getting radio airplay and royalties
content: Submit clean edits with metadata to stations and register works with CMOs for airplay royalties. Track airplay logs. Keep submission and royalty records.

title: Registering copyright step by step
content: Apply to KECOBO with the work copy, applicant IDs, and fees, then collect the certificate. Registration strengthens enforcement. Keep the application, receipt, and certificate.

title: Collecting streaming royalties
content: Register works with MCSK, KAMP, and PRISK as applicable and declare releases for collection. Track statements per work. Keep membership and declaration records.

title: Sampling other recordings
content: Samples need clearance from master and publishing owners with fees. Uncleared samples invite takedowns and suits. Keep clearance letters and payment records.

title: Skiza tunes and caller tunes revenue
content: Skiza deals need written revenue shares, reporting, and audit rights with aggregators. Reconcile statements. Keep contracts and payout records.

title: Stolen social media handles and pages
content: Recover hacked pages through platform verification with IDs and prior admin proof, then report to DCI. Keep admin records and recovery references.

title: Software ownership with developers
content: Code ownership, licences, and escrow belong in written developer contracts with milestones. Keep repositories, contracts, and payment records.

title: Split sheets for collaborations
content: Every session ends with a split sheet naming beatmakers, writers, and percentage shares with signatures. Without it, disputes default to messages. Keep signed splits with project files.

title: Sync licences for adverts and films
content: Sync uses need master and publishing licences with media, term, and fee terms. Clear before broadcast. Keep licences and cue sheets.

title: Filing takedowns that succeed
content: Takedowns need identity, work proof, registration where available, and exact infringing links. File truthfully; false claims attract penalties. Keep case numbers and evidence.

title: Protecting recipes and formulas
content: Guard recipes with NDAs, access controls, and marked confidential documents. Register nothing publicly. Keep signed NDAs and access logs.

title: Filing a trademark at KIPI
content: File with the mark, class, applicant details, and fees, then follow examination and publication. Oppositions have timelines. Keep filing and publication records.

title: Trademark search before branding
content: Search KIPI registers for conflicting marks in the relevant classes before printing packaging. Keep search reports and application receipts.

title: Utility models for smaller inventions
content: Simpler technical improvements may qualify as utility models with shorter terms. File before disclosure. Keep drawings and filing receipts.

title: Videography contracts and footage
content: Video contracts state raw footage ownership, edits, timelines, and payment milestones. Deliver watermarked previews until balance. Keep contracts and delivery logs.

title: Joint and family ownership of motor vehicles — general guidance
citation: General property guidance; Traffic Act, Cap. 403
content: Where a vehicle is bought jointly or with family funds, record each person's contribution and how sale proceeds or use will be shared. NTSA records may show one name, so a side agreement protects the others. Keep contribution proofs and the written co-ownership agreement.

title: Judgments, decrees and enforcement — general guidance
content: After judgment, the successful party extracts a decree and may apply for enforcement if there is no payment or compliance. Enforcement options depend on court rules and the nature of the order. Keep the judgment, decree and enforcement application records.

title: Kadhi Courts personal status matters — general guidance
content: Kadhi courts determine questions of Muslim personal status, marriage, divorce and inheritance where parties are Muslim and submit to jurisdiction. Proceedings apply Islamic law within constitutional limits. Keep marriage, divorce and succession documents for filing.

title: KEBS standards and counterfeits — general guidance
content: Products sold in Kenya should meet Kenya Bureau of Standards requirements with standardisation marks where applicable. Suspected counterfeit, expired, or unsafe goods can be reported to KEBS with samples, receipts, and seller details.

title: KECOBO copyright registration — general guidance
content: Creators can register works with the Kenya Copyright Board for evidence of ownership, increasingly online. Registration supports takedown requests and enforcement. Keep the application, payment receipt, certificate, and the exact files deposited.

title: KRA PIN for business — general guidance
content: Businesses and their responsible officers need KRA PINs for tax registration, invoicing, import, county licences and government tenders. Details such as business name, address and obligations should be kept updated on iTax. Keep the PIN certificate and iTax login details secure.

title: KRA tax compliance — general guidance
content: Businesses need KRA PIN registration, correct invoicing through eTIMS where required, and timely filing to avoid penalties. Disputes have objection and appeal procedures with strict deadlines. Keep returns, assessments, and objection receipts.

title: Labour disputes — general guidance
content: Employees with disputes should document incidents, seek internal resolution, and may contact the county labour office or legal aid for unfair dismissal, wage, or safety issues. Serious disputes go to the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Keep a dated timeline of events.

title: Land Act, 2012
content: The Land Act governs land administration, management and tenure, including leases, licences, compulsory acquisition, and the rights of landlords and tenants in relation to land. Verify tenure type, approvals, and compensation procedure with the registry or Environment and Land Court guidance.

title: Adverse possession claims
content: Long, open, exclusive occupation may ground adverse possession claims with strict proof over many years. Get advice before asserting or conceding. Keep occupation evidence and payment records.

title: Verifying agents and sellers of land
content: Confirm agency registration, written authority from the owner, and registry records before paying deposits. View the land with documents in hand. Keep authority letters and messages.

title: Buying apartments on sectional titles
content: Flats carry sectional unit titles plus shared common property managed by owners corporations. Review service charge and management records. Keep the sectional title and management accounts.

title: Using Ardhisasa for land services
content: Ardhisasa handles searches, transfers, charges, and cadastral maps with eCitizen login and digital payments. Verify parcel numbers before transacting. Keep payment receipts and application references.

title: Beacons and survey disputes
content: Only licensed surveyors should fix or confirm beacons with mutation forms. Moving beacons is an offence. Keep survey reports and mutation records.

title: Boundary suits in the ELC
content: Boundary cases file with titles, searches, survey reports, and demand history in the ELC. Courts may order site visits. Keep pleadings and survey maps together.

title: Land boundaries and disputes — general guidance
content: Verify title deeds, mutation forms, and beacons through an official search and licensed surveyor before fencing or building. Boundary disputes may be resolved through the land registrar, the Environment and Land Court, or alternative dispute resolution. Keep search slips and survey reports.

title: Lodging cautions and restrictions
content: Claimants can lodge cautions warning against dealings pending disputes, with restrictions for stronger protection. Wrongful cautions attract costs. Keep the caution receipt and case filings.

title: Change of user and development permission
citation: Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019
content: Converting agricultural to commercial or multi-dwelling use needs planning approval with public notice. Build only after approval. Keep approval letters and plans.

title: Using title as loan security
content: Charges over land need spousal consent where applicable, valuation, and registration with statutory sale procedures on default. Read the charge before signing. Keep the charge and loan records.

title: Charges and mortgages over land — general guidance
content: A charge is a registered security that lets a lender recover a loan from the land if the borrower defaults, with notice and statutory sale procedures applying. Borrowers should understand interest, default, and redemption rights before signing charge documents. Keep copies of the charge, loan agreement, and all payment receipts.

title: Chief-led boundary settlements
content: Minor boundary disagreements can be settled by chiefs with survey input and written witnessed agreements. Serious or violent cases go to the registrar or ELC. Keep the settlement record.

title: Land owned by companies
content: Company land dealings need board authority and signatory proof with active company status. Check for charges at the registry and BRS. Keep resolutions and search results.

title: Completion statement on land purchase
content: Completion balances price against deposit, duty, fees, and apportionments with a signed statement. Pay through traceable channels. Keep bank slips and the completion statement.

title: Compensation for compulsory acquisition
content: Affected owners claim land value, developments, disturbance, and relocation costs through inquiry with valuations. Object to low awards promptly. Keep titles, valuations, and acquisition notices.

title: Compulsory acquisition and compensation — general guidance
content: The State may compulsorily acquire land for a public purpose but must pay prompt and full compensation to affected owners and occupants following due process. Affected persons are entitled to notice, inquiry, and an opportunity to claim compensation for land, developments, and losses. Keep title documents, valuation records, and all acquisition notices.

title: Consent to transfer charges
content: Some leases and scheme lands need landlord or board consent before transfer. Apply early with the sale agreement. Keep the consent letter with completion documents.

title: Land Control Board consent — general guidance
content: Dealings in agricultural land generally require Land Control Board consent within a strict time limit, failing which the transaction may be void. Attend the board with IDs, title, sale agreement, and consent fees. Keep the consent letter and meeting records.

title: Controlled transactions and Land Control Board consent — general guidance
content: Sales, transfers, leases, charges and subdivisions of agricultural land in a land control area generally need Land Control Board consent within the statutory period. Parties usually apply to the local board for the area where the land lies and attend the hearing together. Keep the application, board letter of consent, and transfer documents.

title: Customary tenure and adjudication
citation: Land Adjudication Act; Community Land Act, 2016
content: Unregistered customary holdings are adjudicated and registered progressively. Follow the local adjudication notices and objections. Keep hearing notices and determination records.

title: Demolition orders and enforcement notices
citation: Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019
content: Unapproved structures attract enforcement and demolition notices with appeal windows. Respond in writing and regularise where possible. Keep notices, plans, and appeal filings.

title: Deposits on land deals
content: Deposits should be recorded with refund terms, timelines, and default consequences, ideally held by advocates. Avoid cash to strangers. Keep deposit agreements and receipts.

title: Discharging a charge after repaying
content: After full repayment, obtain a discharge signed by the lender and register it to clear the title. Confirm the registry record is clean. Keep the discharge and new search.

title: Eviction from land needs a court order
content: Occupants can only be removed through lawful notice and court process, never by demolitions or force. Seek urgent orders where threatened. Keep title proof and demand letters.

title: Spotting fake title deeds
citation: Land Registration Act; DCI fraud guidance
content: Compare paper, seals, parcel numbers, and registry records; fake titles often mismatch TIMS-style green-card history. Insist on registry searches. Keep suspect documents for DCI.

title: Fencing and access road disputes
content: Fences should follow confirmed boundaries and approved access; blocking shared roads invites court orders. Resolve with survey and chief or ELC process. Keep survey reports and demand letters.

title: Forest and public utility land warnings
content: Excisions of forest or utility corridors sold cheaply are usually fraud. Verify gazette status and registry records. Keep search results and survey confirmation.

title: Freehold tenure in Kenya
content: Freehold gives absolute ownership subject to lawful planning and rates. Verify the title type on the deed and registry before buying. Keep the title and search certificate.

title: Gifts of land between family
content: Family gifts need transfer forms, consent where applicable, and registration like sales. Oral gifts are unenforceable. Keep the transfer, consent, and new title.

title: The green card (parcel file)
content: The green card at the registry records every transaction on a parcel. Inspect it during disputes to trace ownership history. Keep copies of entries relied upon.

title: Group ranches and subdivision
citation: Land (Group Representatives) Act; Community Land Act
content: Group ranch subdivisions follow member registers and consent procedures with titles issued per share. Verify membership and minutes. Keep register extracts and titles.

title: Family disputes over ancestral land
citation: Law of Succession Act; ELC guidance
content: Ancestral land sales without heir consent are challenged through succession objections, cautions, and ELC suits. Gather family meeting minutes and heir lists. Keep filings and registry receipts.

title: Subdividing inherited land among heirs
citation: Law of Succession Act; Land Control Act
content: Heirs subdivide only after confirmation of grant with survey, board consent for agricultural land, and new titles per share. Agree boundaries in writing. Keep the confirmed grant and mutation records.

title: Registering long leases
content: Long leases should be registered to bind buyers and lenders with rent, term, and repair terms clear. Keep the registered lease and rent receipts.

title: Leasing out farmland to investors
content: Leasing shambas for farming or masts needs written terms on rent, duration, use, and restoration with registration for long terms. Keep the signed lease and payment records.

title: Creating and registering a land lease — general guidance
content: A lease over registered land in Kenya must generally be in writing and registered to protect a long-term tenant against later buyers or charges. Short leases and key terms such as rent, duration, repair and termination should be clear to both parties before registration. Keep a copy of the signed lease and registration slip.

title: Leasehold tenure and renewals
content: Leaseholds run for fixed terms, commonly 33, 50, or 99 years, with renewal applications before expiry. Check the unexpired term and ground rent. Keep the lease title and renewal records.

title: Legal aid for land grabbing
content: Victims of grabbing or fraudulent transfer facing loss of homes can seek NLAS help with titles, searches, and OB records. The toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Keep all ownership documents.

title: Land held for minors
citation: Law of Succession Act; Land Registration Act
content: Minors hold land through trustees with court supervision; guardians cannot sell casually. Insist on court approval for dealings. Keep trust and court records.

title: Auction of charged land on default
content: Lenders must issue statutory notices and valuations before auctioning charged land. Borrowers can redeem before the fall of the hammer. Keep demand notices, statements, and sale adverts.

title: Subdivision and mutation forms
content: Subdivisions need survey, mutation approval, and registration of new titles with consent fees. Agree in writing who pays costs. Keep approved mutations and new titles.

title: Neighbour trees and developments
content: Overhanging trees, borehole drilling, and storey developments affecting neighbours need approvals and notice. Complain to NEMA and county planning with photos. Keep approvals and reports.

title: Off-plan plots and projects
content: Off-plan buyers should verify approvals, survey plans, and developer track record with phased payments tied to milestones. Visit the site. Keep approvals, plans, and payment schedules.

title: Public land allocations
content: Public land is allocated through the NLC with part-development and use conditions. Unauthorised occupation risks recovery. Keep allotment letters and compliance records.

title: Quarries and soil extraction near homes
content: Quarrying needs mineral and NEMA approvals with blasting safeguards. Affected residents report cracks and dust with dated photos. Keep structural reports and complaint references.

title: County rates clearance before transfer
content: Transfers need county rates clearance certificates showing arrears paid. Sellers usually clear before completion. Keep clearance certificates and receipts.

title: Land rates, ground rent and clearance certificates — general guidance
content: County land rates and national ground rent must generally be up to date before a transfer is registered, evidenced by a rates clearance or rent certificate. Buyers commonly ask sellers to clear arrears and penalties before completion. Keep clearance certificates, receipts, and search results.

title: Land rates and land rent — general guidance
content: Landowners must pay county land rates and national land rent where applicable, and arrears can block transfers. Confirm clearance certificates at the county and lands office before transacting. Keep clearance receipts.

title: Right to redeem charged land
content: Borrowers may clear arrears and costs to stop a sale at any time before completion. Get the redemption figure in writing. Keep payment proof and lender correspondence.

title: Land Registration Act, 2012
content: The Land Registration Act governs registration of interests in land, including transfers, leases and charges, and the effect of registration on proprietors. Always conduct an official search and verify the seller's ID, title deed, and encumbrances before paying.

title: When land disputes go to tribunals
content: Some controlled tenancies and land rent matters start at tribunals before the ELC. Check the forum on the notice received. Keep notices and tribunal filings.

title: Ground rent disputes
content: Unpaid ground rent blocks transfers and attracts penalties. Confirm statements at the lands office and clear arrears before completion. Keep rent receipts and clearance.

title: Riparian reserves and road reserves
citation: Land Act; Water Act, 2016; survey guidance
content: Building on riparian or road reserves risks demolition without compensation. Verify reserves on survey plans before buying or building. Keep survey reports and approvals.

title: Water frontage and borehole permits
content: Abstraction from rivers or boreholes needs Water Resources Authority permits alongside county connections. Illegal connections attract penalties. Keep permits and bills.

title: Land sale agreements and deposits — general guidance
citation: Law of Contract Act; Land Act, 2012
content: Land sale agreements should be in writing with parties, price, payment schedule, completion date, and default terms. Avoid large cash deposits without a lawyer or escrow, and insist on receipts. Keep the agreement, payment proof, and all messages.

title: How to do an official land search
content: Apply with the title number and owner ID through the registry or Ardhisasa, pay the fee, and collect the search showing owner, size, and encumbrances. Keep the search printout with the agreement.

title: Title search and Ardhisasa — general guidance
content: Before buying land, conduct an official title search, confirm rates and land rent are paid, and inspect the land with the seller's documents. Nairobi and other registries increasingly use the Ardhisasa online platform. Keep search certificates and payment receipts.

title: Sectional and strata titles for flats — general guidance
content: Apartments and mixed developments in Kenya can be held on sectional titles with individual unit titles plus shared ownership of common areas. Owners typically belong to an owners corporation that manages common property, insurance, and service charges. Keep your sectional title, management records, and payment receipts.

title: Service charge disputes in estates
content: Demand budgets and audited accounts where service charges seem excessive, then raise disputes through management and the ELC where needed. Keep demand notes and receipts.

title: Spousal consent on land dealings
content: Dispositions of matrimonial land need written spousal consent. Transactions without it are voidable. Keep consent forms with completion documents.

title: Long occupation and settlement schemes
content: Long occupiers should engage settlement and adjudication programmes rather than force. Keep occupation history, chief letters, and programme records.

title: Valuation for stamp duty
content: Government valuers assess duty on transfers; under-declared prices are adjusted upwards. Budget for duty, registration, and advocate fees. Keep valuation reports and duty receipts.

title: Stamp duty and government valuation on transfers — general guidance
content: Most land transfers and leases attract stamp duty assessed on the value or consideration, often after a government valuation. Parties should budget for duty, valuation, registration, and advocate fees before signing agreements. Keep valuation reports, duty payment receipts, and registration records.

title: Transfer by transmission after death
citation: Law of Succession Act; Land Registration Act
content: Heirs transfer land by transmission with the confirmed grant, IDs, and registry forms rather than sale forms. Pay rates clearance first. Keep the new title and grant.

title: Unlawful occupation — general guidance
content: Unlawful occupation or encroachment on land may be challenged through legal action seeking eviction or compensation. Do not use force or demolish structures without a court order. Keep title proof, photos, demand letters, and witness details.

title: Disputing land valuations
content: Valuation disputes are tested with independent registered valuer reports and comparable sales. Commission a second report where figures diverge. Keep both reports and instructions.

title: Wayleaves for power and water lines
content: Utilities may seek registered wayleaves with compensation for lines crossing land. Negotiate terms before construction. Keep wayleave agreements and payment records.

title: Legal Aid Act, 2016
content: The Legal Aid Act establishes the National Legal Aid Service and provides for legal aid in criminal, civil, and constitutional matters, including eligibility, application procedures, and referral to accredited providers. Applications need IDs, case documents, and proof of means where required.

title: Legal aid eligibility in Kenya — general guidance
content: State legal aid prioritises indigent persons, children, persons with disabilities and others facing serious injustice without means to pay. Eligibility is assessed through means and merit tests. Keep income documents and case papers for the assessment interview.

title: Limitation periods general guidance
citation: Limitation of Actions Act; Legal guidance
content: Different claims must be filed within statutory limitation periods, which vary by claim type and tribunal. Time generally runs from when the cause of action arises, subject to legal exceptions. Keep dated documents that show when the dispute arose.

title: Limitation periods — general guidance
content: Civil claims have strict filing deadlines that vary by claim type, and late filing can defeat an otherwise strong case. Criminal reporting should also be prompt to preserve evidence. Note the date the issue arose and verify the applicable deadline with a lawyer immediately.

title: Liquor licensing for outlets — general guidance
citation: Alcoholic Drinks Control Act, 2010; county alcoholic drinks laws
content: Selling alcoholic drinks requires the relevant national and county licences for the premises and hours applied for. Counties enforce location, hours and public health conditions. Keep licences displayed and renewal applications filed early.

title: Limited liability partnership option — general guidance
content: Professionals and small firms may use a limited liability partnership to separate personal liability from firm debts while retaining flexible management. An LLP agreement governs capital, profit sharing and decision making. Keep the LLP agreement and BRS filings with business records.

title: Logbook loans and motor vehicles used as security — general guidance
citation: General lending guidance; Traffic Act, Cap. 403
content: If a logbook is held as security for a loan, the lender's interest may be recorded and the car can be repossessed on default. A buyer who takes such a car without clearance risks losing it to the lender. Keep the NTSA search, loan clearance letter and transfer records.

title: Buying a vehicle with a lost logbook claim — general guidance
content: Do not pay in full for a vehicle whose seller claims the logbook is lost and promises to find it later. Insist on a current NTSA search, police abstract where relevant, and completion of transfer on TIMS. Keep the search, abstract, agreement and transfer messages.

title: LPOs and supply terms — general guidance
citation: General contract guidance; Sale of Goods Act, Cap. 31
content: A Local Purchase Order should state items, quantities, price, delivery date, payment terms and where disputes will be resolved. Suppliers should confirm acceptance and note any conditions before delivery. Keep the LPO, delivery notes and invoices stapled to payment records.

title: Civil cases in Magistrates Courts — general guidance
citation: Civil Procedure Act and Rules; Judiciary guidance
content: Civil suits in magistrates courts begin with a plaint, statement of claim and supporting documents, followed by service and defence. The court may order mediation or case conference before full hearing. Keep filed pleadings and service affidavits in order.

title: Magistrates Courts jurisdiction in Kenya — general guidance
content: Magistrates courts handle most civil and criminal cases at first instance across counties, subject to statutory limits on sentence and claim value. Matters beyond their jurisdiction are referred to the High Court or specialised courts. Keep copies of the charge sheet or plaint and court stamps for reference.

title: Criminal mention and plea in Magistrates Courts — general guidance
content: Criminal cases are first mentioned for plea-taking, bail consideration and directions on disclosure and witnesses. Adjourned mentions track investigations and readiness for hearing. Keep the bail order, bond receipts and mention dates recorded.

title: Marriage registration — general guidance
content: Kenya recognises civil, customary, Christian, Hindu, and Islamic marriages, each with registration requirements. Registration protects property and succession rights. Keep the marriage certificate, and for customary marriages, evidence of rites and witnesses until registered.

title: Matrimonial property — general guidance
content: Matrimonial property is generally shared based on contribution, and each spouse's monetary and non-monetary contribution counts. Keep title deeds, loan statements, receipts for improvements, and records of domestic contribution for division proceedings.

title: Mentions and directions conferences — general guidance
content: Mentions and pre-trial directions confirm service, pleadings, documents and readiness for hearing. The court sets timelines for disclosure, statements and mediation. Keep the directions order and compliance checklist updated.

title: Mobile loans and CRB listing — general guidance
citation: Central Bank of Kenya guidance; CRB Regulations
content: Digital lenders must disclose fees and interest, and borrowers listed with credit reference bureaus must be notified. Request your clearance certificate, dispute errors in writing, and keep loan statements and repayment proof. Verify current CBK licensing of the lender.

title: Motor vehicle sale fraud red flags — general guidance
citation: NTSA guidance; General fraud awareness guidance
content: Be cautious of prices far below market, rushed sales, sellers who avoid TIMS transfer, mismatched names, or requests for deposits to strangers. Always meet at a safe place, verify IDs, and complete transfer and payment through traceable channels. Keep messages, adverts, IDs and payment records if you need to report.

title: Compulsory motor insurance in Kenya — general guidance
citation: Insurance Act, Cap. 487; Traffic Act, Cap. 403
content: Every motor vehicle used on a public road must have at least third-party motor insurance from a licensed insurer. Driving without valid cover can lead to fines, impounding and personal liability for accident damage. Keep the insurance certificate, policy schedule and renewal receipts in the vehicle file.

title: Motor insurance when buying or selling a vehicle — general guidance
citation: Insurance Act, Cap. 487; Insurance Regulatory Authority guidance
content: Motor insurance does not automatically transfer with the logbook, so the new owner should arrange fresh cover before driving the vehicle. The seller should notify their insurer of the sale to stop future liability. Keep the new cover note, policy documents and cancellation or notification letters.

title: NTSA motor vehicle search before buying — general guidance
content: Before paying for a used car, do an NTSA search to confirm the registered owner, engine and chassis numbers, and whether any loan or caveat is recorded. Do not rely on a photocopy logbook or the seller's word alone. Keep the search result printout and the seller's ID details.

title: M-Pesa andSIM-swap fraud — general guidance
citation: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, 2018; CBK guidance
content: For mobile money fraud, immediately reverse where possible, call the provider to freeze, report to police and DCI with transaction IDs, and notify your bank. Keep SMS records, transaction codes, and call reference numbers. Never share PINs or OTPs.

title: Micro and small enterprises support — general guidance
content: The Micro and Small Enterprises Authority supports registration, worksites, market access and capacity building for small traders and artisans. County governments may designate worksites and markets for MSEs. Keep MSE registration and worksite allocation letters for enforcement checks.

title: Stolen beats and songs — general guidance
content: If someone used your beat or song from YouTube without permission, preserve the original project files, timestamps, upload dates, messages, and split sheets showing producers and writers. Options include platform takedown, demand letters, collective management organisations, and KECOBO or court enforcement. Note that beats given away or sold may carry licence terms.

title: National Legal Aid Service — legal aid services
content: The National Legal Aid Service provides legal advice, representation, and alternative dispute resolution support to qualifying persons. Its toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Contact the nearest centre with IDs and all case documents.

title: Client non-payment — general guidance
citation: General contract and small claims guidance
content: For unpaid invoices, send a written demand with the contract, delivery proof, and deadline, then consider mediation or small claims. Keep timesheets, delivery evidence, messages acknowledging the debt, and payment records.

title: Hakili is not a lawyer — general guidance
content: Hakili prepares checklists and organises information from verified passages and user documents. It does not give legal advice or predict outcomes. Confirm every plan with a qualified lawyer, paralegal, or the National Legal Aid Service before acting.

title: NSSF contributions for staff — general guidance
content: Employers must register with NSSF, deduct employee contributions where applicable and remit employer and employee contributions by the due date. Late remittance attracts penalties and interest under the Act. Keep NSSF returns and payment receipts with payroll.

title: NSSF and SHIF deductions — general guidance
citation: NSSF Act, 2013; Social Health Insurance Act, 2023
content: Employers must remit statutory deductions including NSSF and the Social Health Insurance Fund where applicable, and employees should receive payslips showing deductions. Check remittance statements and raise missing remittances with the employer, then the fund or legal aid.

title: NTSA licensing and inspection — general guidance
citation: National Transport and Safety Authority Act, No. 33 of 2012
content: Driving licences, vehicle registration, inspection, and PSV licensing run through the National Transport and Safety Authority, increasingly online. Keep NTSA receipts, inspection stickers, and licence records for enforcement or accident follow-up.

title: Number plates and motor vehicle identity — general guidance
content: Registration plates should match the logbook and TIMS record, be properly fixed, and not be obscured or altered. Mismatched or temporary plates without documents are a warning sign. Keep photos of plates, chassis plates and the NTSA search.

title: Police OB and abstracts — general guidance
content: Always obtain the Occurrence Book number when reporting, and request abstracts or P3 forms where needed for insurance, medical, or court use. Follow up with the investigating officer's name and contacts. Keep copies of every document issued.

title: ODPC complaints — general guidance
content: Individuals whose data is misused can complain first to the organisation holding the data, then to the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner with evidence and reference numbers. Keep screenshots, messages, and the organisation's response for the complaint file.

title: Online harassment and intimate images — general guidance
content: Sharing intimate images without consent, cyberbullying, and threats are offences. Preserve links, screenshots with timestamps, and account handles, report to the platform and police, and seek support services. Requests for intimate content from strangers should be blocked and reported.

title: P3 medical examination form — general guidance
citation: National Police Service and health guidance
content: In assault or injury cases, police issue a P3 form for examination and documentation by a medical officer. The completed form supports investigation and prosecution. Keep a copy of the issued and returned P3 records.

title: Forming a partnership and partnership deed — general guidance
content: A partnership arises where persons carry on business in common with a view to profit, and a written partnership deed records capital, profit sharing, duties and exit terms. Partners are generally jointly liable for partnership obligations incurred in the ordinary course. Keep a signed deed and records of contributions and drawings.

title: Partnerships and chama agreements — general guidance
content: Put partnership and chama terms in writing: contributions, profit sharing, signatories, withdrawals, and dispute resolution. Joint bank accounts need clear mandates. Keep minutes, statements, and receipts for every contribution.

title: Patents, utility models and designs — general guidance
content: Technical inventions, utility models, and industrial designs are registered through the Kenya Industrial Property Institute with novelty and disclosure requirements. Public disclosure before filing can destroy novelty. Keep lab books, drawings, and filing receipts confidential until advised.

title: PAYE for employers — general guidance
citation: Income Tax Act, Cap. 470; Tax Procedures Act, 2015
content: Employers who pay emoluments must register as employers with KRA, deduct PAYE and remit it by the due date with monthly returns. Annual employer reconciliations and P9 forms support employees' tax filings. Keep payroll, remittance receipts and P9 copies.

title: Payment proof for motor vehicle purchase — general guidance
content: Pay by bank transfer, banker's cheque or mobile money with a clear reference, not cash without a receipt, so you can prove who was paid and for which vehicle. Match the payee name to the registered owner or their documented agent. Keep bank slips, M-Pesa statements and signed acknowledgements of payment.

title: Penal Code (Cap. 63)
content: The Penal Code defines criminal offences in Kenya and their penalties, including assault, theft, fraud, and property offences, and sets out general principles of criminal liability. Criminal cases are prosecuted by the State through the Director of Public Prosecutions; victims report to police and keep OB numbers, medical reports, and receipts.

title: Police OB entry and police abstract — general guidance
content: Incidents such as accidents, loss or assault should be reported promptly at a police station for entry in the Occurrence Book. A police abstract summarises the report for insurance or court use. Keep the OB number and abstract copy safely.

title: Securing M-Pesa and bank accounts
content: Use PINs, biometrics, and SIM PINs with no sharing of OTPs, and lock SIM swaps with the provider. Keep provider security confirmations.

title: Requesting your data from a company
content: Write to the data controller describing the data sought with ID; they must respond within statutory timelines. Escalate to ODPC where ignored. Keep delivery proof.

title: Agents photocopying IDs at shops
content: Question bulk ID copying at agents and shops; ask the purpose and retention. Sign across copies shared. Keep a log of copies given.

title: Protecting bank statements shared for jobs
content: Share redacted statements where possible and mark the purpose in writing. Demand deletion after review. Keep transmission records.

title: Biometric data at work and gates
content: Fingerprints and face data need explicit consent with secure storage and alternatives. Query necessity in writing. Keep consent and policy records.

title: What to do after a data breach notice
content: Change passwords, enable 2FA, monitor accounts, and preserve breach notices for claims. Report misuse to ODPC and DCI. Keep notices and loss records.

title: Recording calls as evidence
content: Recordings are weighed with consent, disclosure, and authenticity context. Get advice before secret recording. Keep originals with metadata.

title: Home CCTV and neighbours privacy
content: Angle cameras to your property, inform visitors, and secure footage with limited retention. Neighbour complaints go to ODPC. Keep signage photos and retention policy.

title: Workplace CCTV notices
content: Employers must post CCTV notices with purpose and retention, limiting coverage of private areas. Raise objections in writing. Keep notices and policies.

title: Church and chama member lists
content: Groups need consent before publishing member contacts or photos. Request removal in writing. Keep consent and removal records.

title: Valid consent for data collection
content: Consent must be freely given, specific, and informed with clear opt-in, not pre-ticked boxes. Withdraw anytime. Keep consent screens and withdrawal proof.

title: Defamation in WhatsApp groups
content: False group messages harming reputation attract civil and criminal complaints. Preserve full-chat exports with dates, seek retraction first. Keep harm evidence.

title: Deleting your data (right to erasure)
content: Request deletion where data is unnecessary or consent is withdrawn, subject to legal retention duties. Keep the request, response, and confirmation.

title: Doxxing: personal details posted online
content: Request platform removal, tighten account privacy, and report to ODPC and DCI with links. Keep removal requests and references.

title: Your rights over personal data
content: Data subjects can access, correct, delete, object, and withdraw consent with requests to the controller. Respond in writing with ID. Keep request and response copies.

title: Hacked email recovery
content: Recover via provider flows, revoke sessions, and check forwarding rules set by attackers. Warn banks linked to the email. Keep recovery logs.

title: Employer monitoring of staff
content: Workplace CCTV, email, and device monitoring need notice, policy, and proportionality. Challenge covert surveillance in writing. Keep policies and monitoring notices.

title: False publications about you online
content: False online publications are reported to platforms and DCI with links, timestamps, and harm evidence. Keep preservation screenshots before deletion.

title: GPS tracking by employers or spouses
content: Covert vehicle or phone tracking needs lawful basis and notice; challenge misuse in writing. Keep tracking evidence and objections.

title: Hospital records confidentiality
content: Health facilities must keep treatment records confidential with access on consent or court order. Request your records in writing. Keep request and disclosure logs.

title: Hotel guest registers
content: Hotels collect IDs per law but must secure registers and limit access. Query over-collection. Keep booking confirmations.

title: eCitizen and Huduma data safety
content: Use official eCitizen channels with strong passwords and verified agents; never share OTPs. Report misuse with transaction references. Keep payment receipts.

title: Signing across ID copies
content: Write the purpose and date across ID copies shared with agents to deter reuse for loans. Keep a log of copies issued.

title: Blocking a stolen phone by IMEI
content: Request IMEI blocking through the provider and police with box and purchase proof. Keep the box IMEI, receipt, and OB copy.

title: Job applicant data and background checks
content: Background checks need consent with relevant scope; demand to see adverse findings. Keep application copies and consent records.

title: Fake jobs harvesting ID data
content: Scam recruiters collect IDs and fees for nonexistent jobs. Verify premises and registration before sharing documents. Report with adverts and messages.

title: Children safety online
content: Use parental controls, approve apps, and teach reporting of strangers and explicit content. Report exploitation to DCI child units. Keep device and incident logs.

title: KRA PIN used by fraudsters
content: Check iTax for unknown obligations, change credentials, and report to KRA and DCI with affidavits. Keep dispute letters and references.

title: Legal aid for privacy violations
citation: Legal Aid Act; Data Protection Act
content: Victims of serious data misuse can seek NLAS help with evidence and references. The toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Keep the full evidence file.

title: Loan apps accessing contacts
content: Loan apps must limit collection and get consent before contacting your list; report shaming to ODPC and CBK. Keep permission screenshots and abusive messages.

title: Lost phone with mobile money
content: Block the SIM immediately, freeze mobile money, and report to police with IMEI. Remotely secure accounts where possible. Keep OB and provider references.

title: Stopping spam SMS and calls
content: Opt out with STOP codes, block senders, and report persistent spam to CA and ODPC. Keep spam samples and complaint numbers.

title: Getting M-Pesa statements for cases
content: Request certified statements through official channels with ID for the disputed period. Courts admit certified records. Keep request receipts and statements.

title: Filing a complaint with ODPC
content: Complain first to the organisation, then to ODPC with evidence, reference numbers, and timelines. File online with attachments. Keep the complaint reference.

title: Never share OTPs with callers
content: Banks, Safaricom, and KRA never ask for OTPs by phone. End suspicious calls and verify via official channels. Keep call details for DCI reports.

title: Password and account recovery hygiene
content: Use unique passwords with authenticator backups and updated recovery contacts. Store sparingly offline. Keep recovery codes safely.

title: Spotting phishing messages
content: Fake KRA, bank, and delivery links harvest credentials; verify sender addresses and never enter PINs via links. Report to providers and DCI. Keep message screenshots.

title: Removing personal data from public posts
content: Request search and platform delisting of exposed IDs, contacts, and addresses with evidence. Keep removal requests and outcomes.

title: Intimate images shared without consent
content: Report to platforms, police, and support services immediately with links and handles; do not engage the poster. Preserve evidence with timestamps. Keep report references.

title: SACCO member data use
content: Societies must limit statements sharing and get consent for marketing. Object to guarantor shaming. Keep objection letters.

title: CCTV in schools
content: Schools need CCTV policies with notices, limited coverage, and secure footage. Raise concerns with the board in writing. Keep policies and incident notes.

title: School records and children data
citation: Data Protection Act; Basic Education Act
content: Schools need parental consent for publishing pupil photos and limit access to records. Object in writing to misuse. Keep consent forms and publications.

title: Debt collectors contacting your family
content: Collectors must not disclose your debt to contacts; report shaming to ODPC and CBK. Keep abusive messages and call logs.

title: SIM replacement fraud prevention
content: Replace SIMs in person with original ID and secret questions; set a SIM PIN after. Report suspicious replacements immediately. Keep agent receipts.

title: Stalking and persistent harassment
citation: Protection Against Domestic Violence Act; Penal Code
content: Log every contact attempt with dates, seek protection orders, and report to police. Keep messages, logs, and witness details.

title: Children images in shows and adverts
content: Using children in adverts needs parental consent with contracts and limited hours. Keep consent forms and contracts.

title: Landlord handling of tenant IDs
content: Landlords should copy only needed ID pages, store securely, and return on exit. Object to sharing with third parties. Keep handover records.

title: Hacked WhatsApp accounts
content: Alert contacts, re-verify with SMS codes, enable two-step verification, and report fraud to contacts and DCI. Keep recovery records.

title: Public Wi-Fi safety
content: Avoid banking on open Wi-Fi, use VPNs, and verify hotspot names with staff. Log out of shared devices. Keep incident notes where losses follow.

title: Protecting witness contacts
content: Share witness details only with investigators and counsel, redacting where possible. Keep disclosure logs and protection references.

title: Sentencing, probation and community service — general guidance
citation: Probation of Offenders Act; Community Service Orders Act
content: Courts may impose fines, imprisonment, probation, or community service depending on the offence. First-time and minor offenders may be considered for non-custodial sentences. Verify the sentence, payment deadlines, and reporting conditions on the court order.

title: Seeking adjournments properly
content: Request adjournments early with reasons and evidence, serving opponents in advance. Costs may follow. Keep the application and order.

title: Commissioning affidavits correctly
content: Deponents swear before commissioners with IDs, stating facts within knowledge. False statements are perjury. Keep commissioned originals.

title: Appeal timelines are strict
content: Appeal windows run from judgment with short days for different courts. Instruct counsel immediately. Keep the judgment and filing receipts.

title: Assessors in serious trials
content: Serious trials may use assessors advising on facts with the judge deciding. Follow directions on evidence. Keep trial notes.

title: Applying for bail or bond
content: Apply with IDs, sureties, and address proof; courts weigh flight risk and gravity. Keep the bail order and receipts.

title: Filing at the Business Premises Tribunal
content: Protected tenancy disputes file with leases, notices, and payment records following statutory notice. Keep tribunal orders.

title: Preparing a trial bundle
content: Arrange pleadings, statements, exhibits, and authorities paginated with an index. Bring originals and copies. Keep the indexed bundle.

title: Tracking cases online
content: Follow case numbers for mentions, directions, and judgments on judiciary channels. Attend despite online updates. Keep hearing notices.

title: Using chief letters as evidence
citation: Evidence Act; succession and land practice
content: Chief letters support heir and boundary facts but need corroboration in court. Verify contents before filing. Keep the stamped letter and verification notes.

title: Filing in Children's Court
content: Custody, maintenance, and protection matters file with birth records and prior orders through children officers. Keep filings and officer reports.

title: Computing court timelines
content: Count clear days excluding filing day per rules, watching weekend and holiday shifts. Diarise every deadline from orders. Keep a limitation diary.

title: Contempt of court consequences
content: Disobeying orders or disrupting courts attracts fines and jail. Comply or appeal; never ignore. Keep orders and compliance proof.

title: Filing at the Co-operative Tribunal
content: SACCO and society disputes file with by-laws, statements, and demand history. Keep pleadings and orders together.

title: Extracting decrees and orders
content: Extract the sealed decree after judgment for enforcement with approved costs. Check names, dates, and orders. Keep the sealed decree.

title: Setting aside default judgments
content: Defaults from missed service or deadlines can be set aside with explanation and draft defence, promptly. Keep service records and the draft defence.

title: Demand letters before filing suit
content: Send a dated demand with amount, basis, and deadline by traceable means. Many disputes settle here. Keep the demand and delivery proof.

title: Creating a judiciary e-filing account
content: Register with ID, email, and phone, then verify before filing. Keep login details secure and receipts for payments.

title: Executing decrees: options
content: Execution runs through attachment, garnishee, or sale with warrants and notices. Choose the viable asset. Keep warrants and sale records.

title: Marking and producing exhibits
content: Originals are marked sequentially with copies for the court and opponents. Photos, messages, and receipts need authentication. Keep exhibit lists.

title: Chain of custody for exhibits
content: Exhibits need sealed handling with movement logs from scene to court. Breaks weaken cases. Keep exhibit receipts.

title: Fee waivers for those who cannot pay
citation: Judiciary fees guidance; Legal Aid Act
content: Fee waivers or legal aid cover apply on means proof for qualifying persons. Apply early with income evidence. Keep waiver decisions and receipts.

title: Paying court fines in instalments
content: Request time to pay with income proof where lump fines are impossible. Default risks warrants. Keep the order and payment receipts.

title: Garnishee orders on bank accounts
content: Courts can order banks holding debtor funds to pay the decree holder. Attack or defend with account evidence. Keep the order and bank records.

title: Identification parades
content: Parades follow regulated line-ups with counsel present for suspects. Witnesses identify without coaching. Keep parade records.

title: Temporary injunctions to stop harm
content: Injunctions need a prima facie case, irreparable harm, and balance of convenience with full disclosure. Breach is contempt. Keep the application and order.

title: Interpreters in court
content: Request interpretation early where language barriers exist; proceedings must be understood. Keep request records and hearing notes.

title: Judicial review leave stage
citation: Fair Administrative Action Act; JR procedure
content: Judicial review starts with leave showing an arguable case against a public body, filed promptly. Keep the decision, demand history, and leave papers.

title: Judicial review remedies
content: Courts quash unlawful decisions, compel action, or prohibit excess with declarations. Seek interim stays where harm looms. Keep orders and compliance notes.

title: Filing in Kadhi courts
content: Muslim personal matters file with marriage, birth, and succession documents where parties submit. Keep filings and orders.

title: What happens at mentions
content: Mentions confirm service, compliance, and hearing readiness with directions and dates. Attend every mention. Keep the directions order and diary.

title: Plea agreements in court
content: Negotiated pleas go through counsel, victim input, and court approval with voluntariness checks. Keep the agreement and court record.

title: Plea taking in criminal cases
content: Charges are read in an understood language with guilty, not-guilty, or mute pleas recorded. Understand consequences before pleading. Keep the charge sheet.

title: Pre-trial conferences and settlement
content: Courts narrow issues and explore settlement before trial with document bundles. Prepare chronologies and offers. Keep conference notes and orders.

title: Probation reports before sentence
content: Courts call social inquiry reports on background and reform prospects. Cooperate with probation officers. Keep the report and sentence records.

title: Records of appeal compilation
content: Appeals need pleadings, judgment, proceedings, and grounds bound as records. Order proceedings early. Keep the filed record.

title: Filing at the Rent Tribunal
content: Controlled tenancy matters file on prescribed forms with agreements and receipts. Keep filings and orders.

title: Review of judgments for error
content: Review lies for errors apparent or new evidence with timelines. Distinguish from appeal. Keep the judgment and review application.

title: Scanning documents for e-filing
content: Scan clearly in PDF under size limits with correct orientation and labels. Rejected uploads delay cases. Keep digital and printed copies.

title: Mitigation before sentencing
content: Mitigate with remorse, restitution, family, and reform evidence after conviction. Prepare records and sureties. Keep the mitigation bundle.

title: Affidavits of service done right
content: Process servers record time, place, and recipient of service with annexed documents. Defective service stalls cases. Keep the affidavit and server contacts.

title: Recording statements with police
content: Give truthful statements, read before signing, and keep a copy of the OB entry. Correct errors promptly. Keep statement copies.

title: Stay of execution pending appeal
content: Stays need prompt applications showing arguable appeal and security. File before execution completes. Keep the stay application and order.

title: Substituted service where respondents hide
content: Courts allow newspaper, notice board, or electronic service where personal service fails, on application with attempts evidence. Keep attempt logs and the court order.

title: Suing the government: notice
content: Claims against government need pre-action notice with particulars before filing. Observe the notice period. Keep the notice and delivery proof.

title: Standing as a surety
content: Sureties pledge assets or cash with ID and attendance duties. Understand forfeiture risks. Keep surety documents and hearing dates.

title: Appealing to the Tax Appeals Tribunal
content: Appeal objection decisions within timelines with assessments and objection history. Keep assessment, objection, and appeal records.

title: Protecting vulnerable witnesses
content: Courts allow screens, video links, and closed sessions for vulnerable witnesses on application. Apply early. Keep the application and order.

title: Search warrants: what to check
content: Check the warrant address, scope, date, and issuing court, then observe and record the search. Do not obstruct. Keep the warrant copy and inventory.

title: Choosing the right court or tribunal
content: Match the dispute to magistrates, Small Claims, ELC, ELRC, or tribunals by subject and value. Wrong forums waste fees and time. Confirm jurisdiction before filing.

title: Witness statements and summons
content: File signed witness statements early and summon reluctant witnesses through court process. Prepare witnesses on procedure, not testimony. Keep statements and summons.

title: Witness expenses and allowances
content: Budget transport and subsistence for witnesses with receipts for taxation. Keep expense records and summons.

title: Reporting corruption to EACC — general guidance
citation: Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission Act; Anti-Corruption and Economic Crimes Act, 2003
content: Bribery, embezzlement, and abuse of office in Kenya can be reported to the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission through its offices and reporting channels. Reporters should give clear dates, persons, amounts, and supporting documents where available. Keep copies of reports and reference numbers.

title: Police and public-service oversight through IPOA, CAJ and KNCHR — general guidance
citation: Independent Policing Oversight Authority Act; Commission on Administrative Justice Act
content: Complaints about police misconduct go to IPOA, complaints about unfair public administration go to the Commission on Administrative Justice, and human rights violations can go to the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights. Each body can receive written complaints and track investigations. Keep OB numbers, complaint references, and supporting evidence.

title: PSV and boda boda incidents — general guidance
content: For matatu and boda boda incidents, record the registration, SACCO or stage, driver details, and route, plus photos and witness contacts. Report to police and the SACCO or owner, and notify the insurer. Keep treatment and fare or delivery records.

title: Public health enforcement in food premises — general guidance
citation: Public Health Act, Cap. 242; Food, Drugs and Chemical Substances Act, Cap. 254
content: Food handlers and eateries must meet hygiene standards, medical examination and premises requirements enforced by public health officers. Officers may inspect, order closure of non-compliant premises or prosecute. Keep medical certificates, inspection reports and compliance notices.

title: Rent increases and deposits — general guidance
citation: Rent Restriction Act, Cap. 296; general tenancy law
content: Rent increases must follow the tenancy terms and applicable law, with written notice. Deposits should be receipted and refundable subject to arrears or damage. Challenge unfair increases through negotiation, tribunal, or legal aid with the agreement and payment history.

title: Rent disputes forum — general guidance
citation: Rent Restriction Act; Business Premises Rent Tribunal guidance
content: Certain controlled tenancies and protected business premises fall under specialised tribunals for rent and eviction disputes. Check whether the premises are controlled or protected before filing in court. Keep the letting agreement and tribunal filings.

title: Rent Tribunal for residential tenancies — general guidance
content: The Rent Tribunal handles controlled residential tenancies, including rent assessment and eviction approvals where applicable. Landlords and tenants file prescribed forms with tenancy agreements and rent receipts. Keep rent receipts and tribunal orders safely.

title: Repairs and uninhabitable houses — general guidance
citation: General tenancy law; Public Health Act
content: Landlords must keep premises in a habitable state and handle structural repairs, while tenants report defects promptly in writing. For serious hazards such as sewage or unsafe wiring, also report to public health. Keep dated photos, repair requests, and receipts.

title: Reporting crime: OB, DCI and ODPP — general guidance
content: Report crime at the nearest police station and obtain the OB number. Serious or cyber-enabled cases may be escalated to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations. Prosecution decisions rest with the Director of Public Prosecutions. Keep OB numbers, statements, and exhibit receipts.

title: Joining and borrowing from a SACCO — general guidance
citation: SACCO Societies Act, 2008; Co-operative Societies Act, Cap. 490
content: SACCO membership requires admission under the by-laws, share contributions and deposits that secure borrowing multiples. Loans require application, appraisal and guarantors under the credit policy. Keep the membership statement, loan agreement and guarantor forms.

title: SACCO loans and dividends — general guidance
content: SACCO disputes about loans, guarantees, or dividends should start with statements and the SACCO's internal dispute process, then the regulator or tribunal. Keep payslips showing deductions, loan forms, and guarantor records.

title: Salary advances and staff loans — general guidance
content: Salary advances and staff loans should be in writing stating amount, repayment instalments and how balances are treated on exit. Statutory limits on deductions from wages protect minimum take-home pay. Keep signed advance forms and payroll deduction records.

title: Salary advances and employer loans — general guidance
content: Employer loans and advances must be documented with instalments and lawful deduction limits on payslips. On exit, final dues set-off must be itemised. Keep the loan form, payslips, and clearance records.

title: Motor vehicle sale agreement — general guidance
citation: Law of Contract; Traffic Act, Cap. 403
content: Put every motor sale in a written agreement with full names, ID numbers, vehicle registration, engine and chassis numbers, price, payment schedule and handover date. Both buyer and seller should sign, with witnesses where possible. Keep signed copies for each party and any payment receipts attached.

title: Sale of goods and fitness for purpose — general guidance
content: Goods sold in the course of business carry implied terms about description, quality and fitness for disclosed purposes. Rejection and remedies depend on the contract and whether defects were discoverable on inspection. Keep delivery notes, inspection records and complaint correspondence.

title: Second-hand motor vehicle buyer risks — general guidance
citation: Traffic Act, Cap. 403; Consumer Protection Act, 2012
content: Used cars may have hidden loans, unpaid duty, altered mileage, accident damage or forged documents. Inspect the vehicle, compare physical engine and chassis numbers with the logbook, and verify service history. Keep inspection reports, photos and all seller representations in writing.

title: Service of summons and pleadings — general guidance
content: Court documents must be served on the other party personally or through permitted substituted service, followed by an affidavit of service. Proper service allows the case to proceed to hearing. Keep the process server affidavit and delivery notes.

title: Sexual Offences Act, 2006
content: The Sexual Offences Act defines sexual offences, penalties, victim support, and reporting procedures. Survivors should seek safety and medical care promptly, report to police, and preserve evidence. Support includes psychosocial care, P3 medical forms, and legal aid referral.

title: SHIF contributions for staff — general guidance
content: Employers and employees participate in the Social Health Insurance Fund under the current SHIF framework, with contributions remitted through the designated system. Registration and timely remittance keep staff cover active. Keep registration details and monthly remittance confirmations.

title: Shop and business premises leases — general guidance
citation: Landlord and Tenant (Shops, Hotels and Catering Establishments) Act, Cap. 301
content: Protected business premises have tribunal safeguards on rent increases, termination, and eviction. Get leases in writing with rent, term, renewal, and goodwill terms. Keep the lease, payment records, and tribunal filings.

title: Shop and stall lease terms — general guidance
content: A shop lease should record rent, deposit, service charge, term, renewal, repair duties and notice for termination. Oral premises agreements are hard to enforce, so key terms should be written and signed. Keep the signed lease, rent receipts and repair requests.

title: Small claims for unpaid supplies — general guidance
content: Liquidated business debts within the court's monetary jurisdiction may be filed in the Small Claims Court for faster hearing. Claimants should bring contracts, LPOs, delivery notes, invoices and demand letters. Keep originals and copies ready for filing and service.

title: Filing a claim in Small Claims Court — general guidance
citation: Small Claims Court Act; Judiciary guidance
content: Small Claims Courts resolve low-value civil disputes through simplified forms and shorter timelines, subject to the statutory limit. Claims are filed at designated registries with contracts, receipts or demand letters attached. Keep copies of the claim form and payment receipts.

title: Small Claims hearing and enforcement — general guidance
citation: Small Claims Court Act; Judiciary guidance
content: Hearings are informal and parties generally appear without complex procedure, with judgment often delivered promptly. If the debtor does not pay, the decree may be enforced through court process. Keep the judgment and decree for enforcement purposes.

title: Small Claims Court — general guidance
citation: Small Claims Court Act, No. 2 of 2016
content: Small Claims Courts handle certain civil disputes up to a statutory monetary limit through simplified, faster procedure. Confirm current jurisdiction, filing fees, and whether the claim type qualifies before filing. Keep contracts, receipts, and demand letters.

title: Stolen motor vehicle checks — general guidance
citation: Traffic Act, Cap. 403; National Police Service guidance
content: A stolen vehicle remains the property of the true owner even if you paid for it, and it can be recovered by police. Check that chassis and engine numbers are original and not tampered with, and verify ownership through NTSA. Keep search results, agreement copies and seller contacts.

title: Administrator accounts and distribution
content: Administrators must collect assets, pay debts, and file accounts before distribution per the confirmed grant. Beneficiaries can demand accounts. Keep inventory, bank records, and the confirmation order.

title: Adopted children inheritance rights
citation: Law of Succession Act; Children Act
content: Legally adopted children inherit as children of the adopter with court orders as proof. Informal stays do not confer succession rights. Keep the adoption order and birth records.

title: Bank accounts of the deceased
citation: Law of Succession Act; banking practice guidance
content: Banks freeze accounts on notification of death and release funds to administrators with the grant. Small balances may have simplified procedures. Keep statements, IDs, and the death certificate.

title: Registering a caution on estate land
content: Beneficiaries fearing disposal can lodge cautions or restrictions at the registry pending succession. The caution warns buyers and requires court removal. Keep the caution receipt and succession filings.

title: Getting the chief's introduction letter
content: The chief lists the deceased, spouses, children, parents, and assets after verifying IDs and consulting family. Attend with IDs, death certificate, and asset documents. Keep the stamped letter and attendance notes.

title: Codicils: small changes to a will
content: Minor changes use a codicil executed with the same formalities as a will and read together with it. Store codicils with the original will. Keep a consolidated list of bequests for executors.

title: Customary land and succession consent
citation: Community Land Act, 2016; Law of Succession Act
content: Community and ancestral land succession needs community assembly consent in addition to court grants. Verify registration status with the community register. Keep consent minutes and grant copies.

title: Daughters equal inheritance rights
citation: Law of Succession Act; Constitution, Art. 27
content: Daughters inherit equally with sons; customary exclusion of daughters is unconstitutional. Challenge discriminatory distributions through objections and court. Keep heir lists and distribution proposals.

title: Death certificate for succession
citation: Births and Deaths Registration Act, Cap. 149
content: Succession cannot start without the death certificate from civil registration. Apply with burial permit and IDs. Keep several certified copies for banks, lands, and courts.

title: Settling estate debts before sharing
content: Loans, taxes, and funeral costs rank before beneficiaries. Administrators advertise for creditors and verify claims. Keep loan statements, demand letters, and payment records.

title: Widow eviction by in-laws: urgent action
citation: Law of Succession Act; Protection Against Domestic Violence Act
content: Evicting or dispossessing a widow without succession process is unlawful. Seek chief intervention, cautions at the lands registry, and urgent court orders. Keep marriage, death, and property documents.

title: Risks of handwritten DIY wills
content: Handwritten wills often fail on attestation, vague gifts, or missing residuary clauses. Have a lawyer review before signing. Keep drafts and the review notes.

title: E-filing succession causes
content: Succession causes are filed on the judiciary portal with petitions, chief letters, IDs, and asset lists. Pay assessed fees and track the case number. Keep digital receipts and stamped pleadings.

title: Terminal dues where an employee dies
content: Families claim unpaid salary, leave, and gratuity from the employer with death certificate and administrator letters. Demand an itemised statement. Keep payslips and payment records.

title: Choosing executors and trustees
content: Name trustworthy executors and alternates who can obtain probate, pay debts, and distribute. Brief them on asset locations and debts. Keep executor contacts with the will.

title: Assets abroad in Kenyan succession
citation: Law of Succession Act; private international law
content: Foreign property may need resealing or parallel proceedings where situated. Disclose all cross-border assets to the advocate. Keep foreign titles and grant copies.

title: Funeral expenses from the estate
content: Reasonable funeral and burial costs are paid from the estate with receipts. Disputes over extravagance are resolved by administrators and the court. Keep all expense receipts.

title: Naming guardians for minors in a will
citation: Law of Succession Act; Children Act, 2022
content: Wills should name guardians and trustees for minor children with maintenance directions. Courts prioritise the child's welfare in confirming arrangements. Keep guardian contacts updated.

title: Life insurance claims after death
content: Beneficiaries claim life cover with death certificate, policy, IDs, and claimant proof. Notify the insurer promptly. Keep policy documents and claim references.

title: Intermeddling with estate property is an offence
content: Selling, renting, or wasting estate property before a grant is intermeddling punishable by courts. Report to the chief, police, and succession court. Keep sale evidence and witness details.

title: Children shares in intestacy
content: Children share the intestate estate equally after the spouse's priority, including children born outside marriage who prove dependency. List every child to avoid later objections. Keep birth records.

title: Spouse share where there is no will
content: Surviving spouses take priority shares of intestate estates with children sharing the remainder per statutory tables. No distribution should occur before the grant. Keep the chief's letter and heir list.

title: Jointly owned property and survivorship
citation: Land Registration Act; Law of Succession Act
content: Joint tenancy may pass outside the will by survivorship while tenancy in common shares fall into the estate. Confirm the title type before drafting. Keep the title deed and search.

title: Legal aid for succession disputes
content: Indigent heirs facing dispossession can seek NLAS help with IDs, death certificate, and property documents. The toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Keep means and case documents ready.

title: Life interest for surviving spouses
content: Surviving spouses may hold life interests in the matrimonial home with remainder to children. The interest ends on remarriage in some cases. Keep the grant wording and property records.

title: Succession where a person is missing
citation: Law of Succession Act; presumption of death guidance
content: Estates of long-missing persons need presumption-of-death orders after police and gazette processes. Report the disappearance with OB records first. Keep search evidence and court orders.

title: Mobile money of a deceased person
content: Mobile money balances form part of the estate claimed with death certificate, administrator grant, and IDs. Report the death to the provider early. Keep transaction statements and claim references.

title: Muslim widow shares and iddah maintenance
citation: Islamic law of succession; Kadhi Courts Act
content: Muslim widows take fixed Quranic shares with iddah maintenance considerations through Kadhi courts. File with heir lists and property schedules. Keep marriage and death records.

title: NSSF survivor benefits
content: Survivors claim NSSF benefits with death certificate, claimant IDs, and relationship proof. File at the nearest branch with the member number. Keep claim receipts and correspondence.

title: Objecting to a succession grant
content: Interested persons may object within the gazette period or seek revocation for concealment. File affidavits with heir and asset evidence. Keep gazette copies and filing receipts.

title: Children born outside marriage in succession
citation: Law of Succession Act; Children Act
content: Children born outside marriage who were maintained or acknowledged rank as dependants with provision rights. Paternity evidence and maintenance proof matter. Keep support records and acknowledgements.

title: Parents and siblings where no spouse or child
content: Where the deceased left no spouse or child, parents and siblings take per statutory order. Distant relatives inherit only after closer classes. Keep family tree evidence and IDs.

title: Pension and gratuity on death
content: Death benefits follow scheme nomination forms and trust law, sometimes outside probate. Confirm nominees with the scheme. Keep nomination forms, IDs, and death certificates.

title: Distributing polygamous estates by house
content: Polygamous intestate estates are shared per house with the surviving spouses and children tables. Administrators map each house separately. Keep house lists and asset schedules.

title: Collecting rent from estate property
content: Rent from estate houses or land is estate income accounted by administrators, not personal income. Tenants should pay against receipts to the administrator. Keep tenancy and payment records.

title: Revoking a grant obtained by fraud
content: Grants obtained by hiding heirs or assets can be revoked with the distribution unwound. Apply with concealed-heir evidence. Keep the original filings and new proof.

title: SACCO shares on death of a member
content: SACCO deposits and shares pass to nominees or administrators with death certificate and grant. Guarantor liabilities attach first. Keep statements, nomination forms, and loan records.

title: Second wives and co-wives in succession
citation: Law of Succession Act; Marriage Act
content: Wives under valid customary or Islamic unions are spouses for succession alongside house-specific sharing. List each house with its children. Keep marriage evidence for every union.
