title: Agreements to sell before grant are void
content: Purported sales of estate land before confirmation of grant pass no valid title. Buyers pay at their own risk. Verify the confirmed grant before paying for estate property.

title: SHIF dependant updates after death
content: Update SHIF records after a contributor dies so dependants retain correct cover. Carry the death certificate and household details. Keep updated registration slips.

title: Small estates and simplified process
citation: Law of Succession Act; magistrates jurisdiction
content: Lower-value estates may proceed in magistrates courts with simplified forms. Confirm the current jurisdictional threshold before filing. Keep valuations and asset lists.

title: Stepchildren and maintained dependants
content: Stepchildren maintained by the deceased may claim as dependants even without adoption. Maintenance evidence and household proof decide. Keep school fee and upkeep records.

title: Tax clearance for estates
content: Settle the deceased's tax arrears and obtain clearance before distributing business or rental estates. KRA may raise assessments on unreported income. Keep returns, assessments, and clearance letters.

title: Trusts for minor beneficiaries
citation: Law of Succession Act; Trustee Act
content: Shares for minors are administered in trust for school fees and upkeep until majority, with accounts to the court. Specify trustee powers and reporting. Keep trust accounts and receipts.

title: Formal requirements of a valid will
content: A will must be in writing, signed by the testator, and attested by two competent witnesses present together. Oral and unregistered informal wishes are hard to enforce. Store the original safely and tell executors where it is.

title: Revoking or changing a will
content: Revoke by a new will stating revocation, by codicil, or by deliberate destruction. Marriage can affect earlier wills, so review after life events. Keep every version dated with the latest clearly marked.

title: Storing wills and telling family
content: Keep the original will with an advocate or safe place and tell executors how to find it. Give copies to spouses without marking originals. Keep a one-page asset map with the will.

title: Who can witness a will
content: Witnesses should be adults of sound mind who are not beneficiaries, since gifts to attesting witnesses can fail. Each should sign in the presence of the testator. Keep witness IDs and contacts with the will.

title: Law of Succession Act — overview
content: The Law of Succession Act governs wills and administration of estates of deceased persons, including rights of surviving spouses, children, and dependants. Disputes are handled by the courts through probate or letters of administration. Keep the death certificate, will if any, and asset lists.

title: Chief's letter and beneficiaries — general guidance
content: Succession filings commonly require a chief's letter listing the deceased, spouses, children, and assets, plus IDs and death certificate. Ensure all beneficiaries are listed to avoid later objections. Keep copies of everything filed with the chief and court.

title: Confirmation of grant and distribution — general guidance
content: After a grant is issued, the court confirms it to approve how the estate will be shared among beneficiaries and dependants. No final distribution should occur before confirmation, and administrators must account for all property collected. Keep inventory records, consents, and the confirmation order.

title: Debts of the estate — general guidance
content: Debts of the deceased are settled from the estate before distribution, and creditors must prove their claims. Administrators should advertise for creditors where required and keep loan statements, demand letters, and payment records.

title: Dependant provision claims — general guidance
content: Spouses, children, and other dependants who were maintained by the deceased may apply for reasonable provision from the estate. Applications have strict time limits running from the grant, so seek advice early and keep proof of dependency and maintenance.

title: Applying for a grant and gazette objections — general guidance
content: Applications for grants of representation in Kenya are commonly gazetted so that interested persons can object or claim within the stated period. Applicants should give full and honest disclosure of heirs, assets, and liabilities from the start. Keep gazette notices, filed forms, and proof of service.

title: Intestate succession (no will) — general guidance
content: Where there is no valid will, the estate is distributed according to statutory shares for spouses, children, and other relatives. No one should subdivide or sell the deceased's land before lawful administration. A chief's letter and death certificate are usually required to start the process.

title: Deceased's land and cautions — general guidance
citation: Land Registration Act, 2012; Law of Succession Act
content: Land belonging to a deceased person should not be transferred until succession is completed and the grant confirmed. Beneficiaries fearing disposal may seek cautions or restrictions at the land registry and urgent court orders. Keep title deed copies, search results, and registry receipts.

title: Muslim intestate succession and Kadhi courts — general guidance
content: The estate of a deceased Muslim in Kenya is generally distributed according to Islamic law through the Kadhi courts or the High Court as appropriate. Heirs should identify all spouses, children, and dependants early to avoid later disputes. Keep death certificates, heir lists, and property documents.

title: Grant of probate and letters of administration — general guidance
content: Administrators must obtain a court grant before distributing an estate, then collect assets, pay debts and taxes, and distribute to beneficiaries with accounts. The process involves filing, gazette notice, and confirmation of the grant. Keep filing receipts, gazette copies, and bank records.

title: Wills — general guidance
content: A valid will must meet formal requirements including signature and witnesses, and testators should keep the original safely and tell executors where it is. Dependants left without reasonable provision may apply to court. Verify validity with a lawyer before acting.

title: Supplier and tender disputes — general guidance
citation: Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 (for public tenders)
content: For supply disputes, keep LPOs, delivery notes, invoices, and acceptance records. Public tender disputes have review procedures with short deadlines through the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority. Private disputes follow the contract's dispute clause.

title: Tax Appeals Tribunal procedure — general guidance
citation: Tax Appeals Tribunal Act; KRA guidance
content: Taxpayers aggrieved by tax decisions first object to the Commissioner and may then appeal to the Tax Appeals Tribunal within statutory timelines. Appeals require the decision letter, objection history and tax records. Keep assessment notices and appeal acknowledgements carefully.

title: Objecting to a KRA assessment — general guidance
citation: Tax Procedures Act, 2015; Tax Appeals Tribunal Act, 2013
content: A taxpayer aggrieved by an assessment may lodge an objection with the Commissioner within the statutory period, stating grounds with supporting documents. If dissatisfied with the objection decision, appeal lies to the Tax Appeals Tribunal. Keep assessment notices, objection letters and Tribunal filings with delivery proof.

title: Telecom and internet complaints — general guidance
citation: Kenya Information and Communications Act; CA guidance
content: Billing, bundles, and service quality complaints should first go to the provider's customer care with account and transaction details, then to the Communications Authority if unresolved. Keep screenshots, reference numbers, and M-Pesa statements.

title: Tenant documents to keep
content: Tenants should keep the tenancy agreement, rent and deposit receipts, notices received, repair requests, correspondence with the landlord, and identification documents. These are commonly needed for legal advice or tribunal and court relief.

title: Test drive and mechanical checks — general guidance
content: Test drive the exact vehicle you intend to buy and, where possible, have an independent mechanic inspect the engine, brakes, body and electronics. Note defects and agree in writing who will fix them and at whose cost. Keep the inspection report and any repair commitments.

title: Motor vehicle logbook transfer on NTSA TIMS — general guidance
content: Ownership passes only when the seller initiates the transfer on NTSA TIMS and the buyer accepts it and a new logbook is issued. Both sides need eCitizen and TIMS accounts, and fees are paid through the official government payment channel. Keep sale agreement, payment proof, ID copies and TIMS receipts.

title: Trade secrets and confidentiality — general guidance
content: Recipes, client lists, and processes can be protected through confidentiality agreements and access controls rather than registration. Use written non-disclosure terms with staff and partners. Keep signed NDAs and access logs.

title: Trade Marks Act — overview
content: Business names, logos, and slogans can be protected as trademarks through the Kenya Industrial Property Institute, giving exclusive use in registered classes. Registration requires search, application, and publication. Keep search reports, certificates, and use evidence.

title: First steps after any accident
content: Secure the scene, help the injured, call emergency services, and exchange details. Do not admit liability at the roadside. Keep photos, plates, and witness contacts.

title: P3 forms after road injuries
content: Police issue P3 forms for medical documentation of road injuries. Complete promptly and return to investigators. Keep hospital notes and OB numbers.

title: Drink-driving breath tests
content: Officers may require breath or blood tests where drink-driving is suspected. Refusal has legal consequences. Seek counsel early and note testing details.

title: Insurance assessors and repairs
content: Assessors inspect and approve repair estimates; do not authorise repairs before approval except to secure the vehicle. Keep estimates, approvals, and garage invoices.

title: Boda boda registration and stages
content: Riders need licences, protective gear, and stage registration with SACCO or association records. Keep licences, stage cards, and payment records.

title: Careless and dangerous driving charges
content: Charges grade from careless to dangerous with fines, licence consequences, and jail terms. Defences turn on road evidence and witnesses. Keep scene photos and charge sheets.

title: Cash bail at traffic stops
content: Minor traffic offences may attract cash bail with official receipts and a court date. Demand a receipt for any payment. Keep the bail receipt and charge sheet.

title: Chassis and engine number checks
content: Compare physical stampings with the logbook and TIMS; tampering voids the deal. Walk away where the seller resists verification. Keep search and inspection notes.

title: Notifying insurers after accidents
content: Notify the insurer promptly with abstract, photos, and estimates per policy timelines. Late notice risks repudiation. Keep claim numbers and submission receipts.

title: Pleading in traffic court
content: Understand the charge, consider plea options with counsel, and bring licence, insurance, and inspection documents. Keep the charge sheet and hearing dates.

title: Cyclist and motorbike rider claims
content: Rider claims follow the same abstract, P3, and medical evidence chain with helmet and licence context. Keep repair estimates and treatment records.

title: Fatal accident claims by dependants
citation: Fatal Accidents Act; Law Reform Act
content: Dependants claim lost support with death, dependency, and income evidence. File within limitation with grant and records. Keep OB, post-mortem, and income proof.

title: Choosing a driving school
content: Train at NTSA-licensed schools with written fees, lessons, and test booking terms. Keep receipts and training records.

title: Passengers and drink-driving liability
content: Passengers should avoid drunk drivers and report dangerous driving; owners face liability for entrusting vehicles. Keep trip and report records.

title: Replacing a lost driving licence
content: Lost licences need police abstract, application, and fees for replacement. Report loss promptly. Keep the abstract and application receipts.

title: Duty verification for imports
citation: EAC Customs Management Act; KRA guidance
content: Ask for import entries and duty receipts and verify registration before paying. Unpaid duty cars face seizure. Keep import and TIMS records.

title: Fake insurance stickers
content: Verify stickers with the insurer and IRA before driving off. Fake cover voids claims. Keep verification messages and policy documents.

title: Paying traffic fines officially
content: Pay fines through official court and government channels with receipts, never cash to individuals. Keep the ticket, receipt, and case reference.

title: Foreign licences in Kenya
content: Visitors drive on valid foreign or international permits within allowed periods; residents convert to Kenyan licences. Keep permits and entry records.

title: Helmet and safety gear offences
content: Riders and passengers must wear standard helmets with reflective gear at night. Fines follow non-compliance. Keep receipts for compliant gear.

title: Hit-and-run: victim steps
content: Get care, report immediately, and preserve dashcam, CCTV, fragments, and witness details. Do not chase dangerously. Keep OB and treatment records.

title: Third-party injury claims
citation: Insurance (Motor Vehicle Third Party Risks) Act
content: Injury claims need police abstract, P3 and medical reports, expense receipts, and lost-income proof within limitation periods. Start early with counsel. Keep every bill.

title: Motor vehicle inspection bookings
content: Commercial and PSV vehicles undergo periodic inspection for roadworthiness with stickers. Book early with registration documents. Keep inspection reports and stickers.

title: Driving licence classes in Kenya
content: Licences are classed by vehicle type with tests, medicals, and renewals per class. Drive only the endorsed class. Keep the licence, test records, and renewal receipts.

title: Licence endorsement and suspension
content: Repeat offences attract endorsements and suspension with hearing rights. Defend with records and counsel. Keep offence history and hearing notices.

title: Turnboys and loader injuries
citation: Work Injury Benefits Act; Traffic Act
content: Loader injuries need incident reports, treatment records, and employer compensation filings. Keep employment proof and medical files.

title: Boda loans and repossession
content: Boda hire-purchase needs statements, instalment proof, and repossession notices. Demand the arrears figure in writing. Keep agreements and payment records.

title: New car registration (scratch to plates)
content: Dealers handle KRA duty, registration, and plates with logbook processing. Verify TIMS records before driving off. Keep sale, duty, and registration records.

title: Number plate verification
content: Plates must match the logbook and TIMS record, properly fixed and unobscured. Mismatches signal fraud. Keep plate photos and the search result.

title: Obstruction and illegal parking
content: Obstructing traffic or parking illegally attracts fines, clamping, and towing. Pay through official channels with receipts. Keep the ticket and payment proof.

title: Overloading fines
content: Overloaded lorries face weighbridge fines and offloading with owner and driver liability. Verify load sheets. Keep weighbridge tickets and charge sheets.

title: Own-damage (comprehensive) claims
content: Comprehensive claims need the policy schedule, abstract, and repair evidence with excess deducted. Confirm exclusions like drink-driving. Keep the full claim file.

title: Passenger rights after accidents
content: Passengers claim against the at-fault vehicle cover with tickets, treatment records, and the abstract. Record the plate and SACCO. Keep fare proof and medical files.

title: Pedestrian knock-down claims
content: Pedestrian claims need the abstract, treatment records, and witness details with the offending plate. Report promptly. Keep every medical receipt.

title: Phone use while driving
content: Holding a phone while driving attracts fines and licence action. Use hands-free mounts. Keep the ticket where disputing the facts.

title: Accidents with convoys and GK vehicles
content: Record plate, unit markings, time, and witnesses, then report to police for abstract processing. Claims follow government procedure. Keep OB and treatment records.

title: PSV licensing and SACCO membership
content: PSVs need operator licences, SACCO or company affiliation, and compliant crew with badges. Verify documents before investing. Keep licences and agreements.

title: Renewing driving licences
content: Renew before expiry through NTSA channels to avoid penalties and enforcement. Keep renewal receipts with the licence.

title: Motor sale agreements checklist
content: Agreements record IDs, registration, engine and chassis numbers, price, schedule, and handover with witnesses. Both sides sign. Keep copies and payment receipts.

title: School transport compliance
content: School vans need yellow paint, speed governors, attendants, and vetted drivers with no overloading. Report violations with photos. Keep contracts and fee receipts.

title: Seat belt offences
content: Drivers and passengers must wear belts where fitted. Fines apply per occupant. Keep the charge sheet where disputing fitting or use.

title: Smart driving licence applications
content: Smart licences apply through NTSA with biometrics, medical, and fees. Book early and track the application. Keep booking slips and payment receipts.

title: Speed limits and cameras
content: Limits vary by road class and vehicle type with camera and NTSA enforcement. Fines and licence action follow readings. Keep the charge sheet and calibration queries for counsel.

title: Taxi licensing basics
content: Taxis need registration, inspection, insurance, and licensed drivers with fare transparency. Keep permits and inspection records.

title: Driving test bookings
content: Tests book through NTSA with ID, training proof, and fees. Prepare documents and practise the route. Keep booking slips and results.

title: TIMS transfer step by step
content: The seller initiates transfer, the buyer accepts, fees are paid officially, and a new logbook issues. Both need eCitizen and TIMS accounts. Keep sale, payment, ID, and receipt records.

title: Towed vehicles: recovery steps
content: Locate the yard, verify the offence and fees, pay officially, and inspect for damage before leaving. Keep the ticket, payment receipts, and yard records.

title: Tuk-tuk operating requirements
content: Tuk-tuks need registration, inspection, insurance, and licensed drivers on authorised routes. Keep permits and fee receipts.

title: Driving without insurance
content: Every public-road vehicle needs at least third-party cover; driving uninsured risks fines, impound, and personal liability. Keep the cover note and policy.

title: Driving without a licence
content: Driving unlicensed or outside the endorsed class risks fines, vehicle detention, and insurance repudiation. Get the correct class before driving. Keep test and licence records.

title: Total loss and write-off settlements
content: Write-offs settle on market value less excess and salvage per policy. Compare valuations before accepting. Keep valuation reports and settlement letters.

title: Traffic Act — overview
content: The Traffic Act regulates licensing, vehicle inspection, speed, drink-driving, and careless or dangerous driving, with fines, licence consequences, and possible imprisonment. After any incident, prioritise safety and medical care, then comply with police directions. Keep licence, inspection, and insurance documents.

title: Turnover tax for small traders — general guidance
citation: Income Tax Act, Cap. 470; Finance Acts
content: Small resident businesses whose turnover falls within the statutory band may fall under turnover tax rather than the standard income tax regime, subject to exclusions. Eligibility, rates and filing frequency change by Finance Act and should be confirmed on KRA guidance. Keep sales records and filed returns to support the regime applied.

title: Unlawful eviction — general guidance
content: Self-help eviction, including lockouts or disconnection of utilities without a court order, may be unlawful. Affected tenants can seek legal assistance and may apply for urgent court orders restoring possession. Keep photos, witness contacts, and utility records.

title: Motor vehicle valuation and price checks — general guidance
content: Compare the asking price with similar models, year, mileage and condition to avoid overpaying or falling for a scam price. Consider an independent valuation for expensive vehicles. Keep valuation reports, adverts for comparable vehicles and price negotiation notes.

title: VAT registration and returns — general guidance
content: Businesses making taxable supplies above the registration threshold must register for VAT, charge VAT on taxable supplies and file periodic returns. Input VAT recovery depends on valid tax invoices and proper records. Keep tax invoices, credit notes and VAT returns in sequence.

title: Deadlines must be verified — general guidance
content: Time limits for notices, appeals, complaints, and filings vary widely and change over time. Never rely on memory or hearsay for a deadline. Confirm the current limit with the relevant office, the statute, or a legal aid provider and diarise it.

title: Warranties on second-hand motor vehicles — general guidance
content: Private second-hand sales are often sold as seen, while dealers may offer limited warranties or undertakings about condition. Get any promise about engine, gearbox or roadworthiness written into the agreement with a clear time limit. Keep the agreement, warranty terms and repair records.

title: YouTube and platform takedowns — general guidance
content: Platforms such as YouTube handle copyright complaints with the claimant's details, work proof, and infringing links. File accurately, keep case numbers, and expect counter-notices. False claims carry consequences, so verify ownership and licences first.
